limitations: Static analysis of one build; no radiator temperature was measured in game. The cooled quantity is a native amount × temperature unit; no conversion to joules or watts was recovered.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Each update the motor takes a speed step of at most 2 × |Throttle| RPS and requests |step| × electric_magnitude × force_emitter_max_force × 0.1 in charge: 0.24, 6.6 and 26.25 per RPS of step for the small, medium and large motor.

sections.title: How the update works
sections.body: With s = Throttle clamped to −1…1, the step is Δ = (20 × sign(s) − speed) × |s|, clamped to −2|s| … 2|s|. Δ is dropped when its sign differs from the throttle's, so a motor running faster than 20 RPS in the throttle direction is not held back, while reversing the throttle drives it toward −20. At zero throttle it only coasts. The motor requests |Δ| × electric_magnitude × force_emitter_max_force × 0.1, multiplies Δ by the fraction supplied, adds it, and then keeps 0.995 of its speed. With a shaft link it submits that speed and force_emitter_max_force to its shaft group and takes the group's published speed back. A damaged motor targets 0; the same step sign gate still applies.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: At the full-throttle step of 2, the small, medium and large motor request 0.48, 13.2 and 52.5 per update. While the step stays at that bound, that is 28.8, 792 and 3150 per simulated second; supply limits the actual draw. Per unit of force_emitter_max_force the cost is 0.12, 0.11 and 0.105. The shaft group weights each part's speed by that force, so the small motor pays 1.1429 times and the medium 1.0476 times what the large one pays for the same force-weighted speed change.

sections.title: Battery supply
sections.body: Each full battery lends at most 10 per update to the pool. Without generation or other loads, the full-step requests need 1, 2 and 6 full batteries for the small, medium and large motor; a large motor on one full battery gets at most 0.1905 of its full-step request. A small step near the 20 RPS target asks for much less.

sections.title: What the cost tracks
sections.body: Charge scales with the speed step, not with speed × step. A given RPS change costs the same at low and high shaft speed, so equal charge buys equal force-weighted speed change rather than equal mechanical work. The shaft solver is a weighted average with no torque or inertia in SI units, so it gives no charge-per-joule figure.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Throttle limits the step, not the target speed: the target is always 20 RPS. Without a shaft link the update settles at 19.9 RPS at full throttle. At zero throttle an unlinked motor keeps 0.74 of its speed after one simulated second. Under load, a lower throttle mainly lowers the step and with it the draw. With infinite_batteries on, the draw helper supplies every request and takes no charge. An EMP pulse cuts the motor's supply while its countdown is 300 or more; supply then returns linearly over the next 300 updates, 5 simulated seconds. A weather strike within 100 m (inference: lightning) adds 800, so the motor gets no charge for 500 updates and full charge again after 800, 13.33 simulated seconds. Electricity lists the other EMP sources.

sections.title: Several bridges and loops
sections.body: When gearboxes or clutches join several shaft groups, each group passes its speed to every group it reaches once, along the first path in queue order, scaled by 0.95 × engagement per link. A loop whose ratios agree within 0.9 to 1.1 adds nothing more. A loop whose ratios disagree brakes every group that source reached: their bridge shares are cleared and the source's weight is added with no speed, so the result depends on group order. A link back into the same group at any ratio other than about 1 brakes that group; with nothing else attached it then publishes half its mixed speed each update (Transmission, inference from the decoded rule).

limitations: Static analysis only; charge is in the internal unit. A conversion of internal charge to joules or watts was not recovered.
Reading component offset 0x160 as the Throttle input is an inference from how the update uses it.

The force-weighted comparisons hold within one shaft group. Across gearbox and clutch bridges, loops and links back into the same group, speeds combine by the traversal rule under Transmission. When connector changes rebuild the groups is an open item listed there.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Recharges a stored rechargeable item by drawing 0.01 internal charge per update, 0.6 per simulated second, until the item is full.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Small units take only small handheld equipment, medium units large equipment; connect Electric to charge.

sections.title: Charge draw
sections.body: While a stored item is below full, the rack withdraws up to 0.01 internal charge from its electrical network each update, 0.6 per simulated second. It scales that request by max(0, (300 - EMP) ÷ 300) × the network's charge fraction and takes no more than the pool holds. If the supplied share is above 0.01 the item gains 100 ÷ (60 × T) percentage points that update, where T is the item's recharge time; partial supply above that share charges at full speed. An empty rack and a full item draw nothing, and a rack with no electrical network does not charge.

sections.title: Recharge time per item
sections.body:
From empty to full at full supply, in simulated seconds, and the charge that costs. inventory_class 1 items go in the small rack and class 2 items in the medium rack, matching the racks' own inventory_class:

- Defibrillator (item 9, inventory_class 2): 300 s, 180 charge from empty
- Flashlight (item 15, inventory_class 1): 1500 s, 900 charge from empty
- Night Vision Binoculars (item 17, inventory_class 1): 1200 s, 720 charge from empty
- Oxygen Mask (item 18, inventory_class 1): 30 s, 18 charge from empty
- Radio (item 19, inventory_class 1): 600 s, 360 charge from empty
- Radio Signal Locator (item 20, inventory_class 2): 3000 s, 1800 charge from empty
- Remote Control Unit (item 21, inventory_class 1): 3000 s, 1800 charge from empty
- Strobe Light (item 23, inventory_class 1): 3000 s, 1800 charge from empty
- Strobe Light, Infrared (item 24, inventory_class 1): 3000 s, 1800 charge from empty
- Transponder (item 25, inventory_class 1): 3000 s, 1800 charge from empty
- Radiation Detector (item 30, inventory_class 1): 600 s, 360 charge from empty

The defibrillator turns each full charge into a stored use while it is below its use limit, then charges again, so the listed cost is per use. Diving gear, scuba gear, both space suits and the firefighter breathing set (items 1, 3, 79, 80 and 149) refill through the gas branch instead and draw no charge here.

families.summary: Small, medium and large tanks have 31.25, 187.5 and 703.125 L compartments that exchange with each port's pipe network; liquid pressure stays low until the last 80 L of room fills; contents drift toward ambient temperature with a time constant of 16.7 simulated seconds.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: The tank keeps its own compartment of volume 1.5625 × listed voxels: 3.125, 18.75 and 70.3125 units, 31.25, 187.5 and 703.125 L. Each Stored Fluid port stays on its own pipe network, and the tank exchanges each network with its compartment at bias 0 and factor 1. Tank Content reads 10 × the stored amount, in litres, and Tank Pressure reads atmospheres. Fluid tanks run water component case 8 and drift toward the surrounding temperature by 0.001 per update.

sections.title: Pressure and fill
sections.body: Pressure follows the compartment law, not the fill fraction. The medium and large tanks are above volume 8, so pure liquid in them reads under 0.5 atm until less than 80 L of room is left, then 7.5 atm more per 75 L, 60 when full. The small tank (volume 3.125) reads 60 × amount ÷ 3.125. Gas in the tank counts toward the same pressure.

sections.title: Initial contents
sections.body: A new tank component starts with fluid index 1, diesel, and fill 1. For a liquid other than diesel or jet fuel, the first build adds 0.99 × fill × V of it plus V ÷ 60 of air, split into nitrogen, oxygen and CO2. Inference from the decoded equations: before any exchange that reads about 60.4, 60.9 and 63.5 atm for the three sizes, because the air takes the last 1 % of room. Set to a gas, a fluid tank receives only 0.99 × fill × V ÷ 60 of it, 0.99 atm at full fill.

sections.title: Diesel and jet fuel at spawn
sections.body:
The first-build fill skips diesel and jet fuel. A separate vehicle spawn operation fills them instead, only when its request enables the resource fill. It asks for 0.99 × fill × V of the selected fuel: 30.9375, 185.625 and 696.09375 L for the small, medium and large tank at full fill. On its inventory branch the fuel is capped to the diesel or jet fuel in stock and taken from it, so a tank can spawn part full, or with no fuel when the stock is empty. Off that branch the whole request is added. Either way the tank also gets V ÷ 60 of air. This operation adds to the existing contents and does not clear them.

The fill runs only when the spawn request's fuel-fill byte is set. Request construction clears it and then copies the caller's argument, and the shared spawn job passes a byte from another object, so a fresh spawn does not always fill. One identified path sets it: the Lua call resetVehicleState marks the vehicle's pending request and enables the fuel fill. The stock-capped branch also needs request mode 1, a second request flag, an inventory record and a cleared settings byte. The limitations below cover which workflows and options set them.

sections.title: Saved contents and reset
sections.body:
Fluid and gas tanks share one serializer. It saves the fill-pending flag as spawner_pending and both compartments, contained_volume and contained_volume_secondary. Each compartment keeps vol_0 to vol_12, the 13 species amounts in the internal unit, plus vol_total, temp and rad. The geometric volume is not saved; it is recomputed from the definition without touching the amounts or temperature. A saved temperature is clamped to −273 … 100000 and a non-finite one becomes 0.

A separate reset zeroes both compartments' amounts and totals and sets fill pending again, so the next pending fill treats the tank as new. It leaves the temperature as it was. A new tank starts at 20 °C. The pending fill skips a tank whose fill-pending flag is 0, so a restored 0 keeps the restored contents through that call. A build reconstructs the pipe networks before it runs the pending fill, and the diesel and jet-fuel fill is a separate step with its own request gate. A restored 0 therefore keeps the contents unless a later reset sets fill pending again.

findings.label: Compartment pressure law
findings.detail: All 13 fluid indices (0 to 12) enter only as liquid sum L or gas sum G, with A = L + G. Pure gas reduces to P = 60 × A ÷ V at any volume. Pure liquid in a volume up to 8 (80 L), such as a pipe network of 4, also gives 60 × A ÷ V. Pure liquid above volume 8 gives max(0.5 × A ÷ V, 7.5 × (A − V + 8)): under 0.5 atm until less than 8 (80 L) of room is left, then 7.5 atm per amount (per 75 L) up to 60 at full. Temperature does not enter. Inference from the instruction sequence; degenerate states follow the original SSE arithmetic. Report: investigation/fluids-network.md. For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Re-evaluates its expression only when an input changes; NaN and infinity output 0.

sections.title: How it updates
sections.body: The output updates on an update where x, y or z changed, and only if the expression parsed. Unchanged inputs keep the last result. Function (1 input) and Function (3 inputs) share this case.

sections.title: Expression language
sections.body:
Expressions are evaluated in binary32. The variables are x, y, z, w, a, b, c and d, in input order; a block with fewer inputs supplies 0 for the rest. The constants are pi (π) and pi2 (2π, not π squared). Names are lowercase. A number is decimal digits with at most one decimal point, so 1e3 and 0x10 are not numbers. There are no comparison, Boolean or conditional operators.

Table: Operators, tightest first
| Operators | Meaning | Grouping |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unary + and - | sign | binds tighter than ^, so -x^2 is (-x)^2 |
| ^ | power | right to left: 2^3^2 is 2^9 |
| * / % | multiply, divide, remainder | left to right |
| + - | add, subtract | left to right |

Table: Functions
| Function | Result |
| --- | --- |
| sin, cos, tan | of an angle in radians |
| asin, acos, atan | angle in radians; asin and acos outside -1 … 1 give 0 |
| atan2(y, x) | angle of the point (x, y) in radians |
| sqrt(x) | square root; 0 for negative x |
| abs(x), sgn(x) | magnitude; sign as -1 below 0 and 1 otherwise, so sgn(0) is 1 |
| floor(x), ceil(x) | round down, round up |
| round(x, step) | step × floor(x ÷ step + 0.5); 0 when abs(step) < 1.1920929e-7 |
| min(a, b), max(a, b) | smaller, larger |
| len(x, y), len2(x, y) | sqrt(x·x + y·y), x·x + y·y |
| lerp(a, b, t) | (b − a) × t + a; t is not clamped |
| clamp(x, lo, hi) | min(hi, max(lo, x)); the bounds are not swapped |

Division and % give 0 when |divisor| < 1.1920929e-7, a smaller threshold than the Divide block's 0.000001. ^ uses the Exponent block's guard, so a negative base with an exponent below 1 gives 0. Intermediate results are not cleaned; only the block output turns NaN and infinity into 0.

Setup parses the expression and evaluates it once with every variable 0. A syntax error, a wrong argument count, or more than 32 values on the operand stack at once marks the expression invalid, and the block keeps its last output. Constant expressions such as pi2 are valid without any variable. Microprocessor function nodes use the same language and likewise skip evaluation while their inputs are unchanged or the expression is invalid.

findings.label: Expression operator precedence
findings.detail: The parser assigns precedence ranks (5 here, 4 at 0x1401e4170, 2 at 0x1401e41b7) and pops stacked operators of higher rank (jb at 0x1401e44ef). For * / % + − it also pops equal rank (jbe at 0x1401e469f), so they group left to right; for ^ it keeps equal rank, so power groups right to left. Unary signs bind tighter than power: -x^2 is (-x)^2, and 2^3^2 is 2^9. Parentheses override the ranks and commas separate function arguments. families.summary: Small, medium, large and huge gas tanks have 46.875, 109.375, 984.375 and 3515.625 L compartments; pressure is 60 × amount ÷ volume, and a fresh tank starts at 59.4 atm at full fill.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: The compartment volume is 1.5625 × listed voxels: 4.6875, 10.9375, 98.4375 and 351.5625 units. The single Stored Gas port exchanges its network with the compartment at bias 0 and factor 1. Gas tanks run water component case 0x14 with the same ambient drift as fluid tanks, a time constant of 16.7 simulated seconds.

sections.title: Pressure and readouts
sections.body: Pressure is 60 × stored amount ÷ volume for any gas or gas mixture, so a full compartment reads 60 atm. Tank Content reads 10 × the stored amount. The tooltip's species list multiplies each gas amount by 60 and then 10, 600 per amount; inference: that is the gas's volume in litres at 1 atm. The two readouts differ by a factor of 60 for the same gas.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: A new gas tank selects the air slot; the editor offers air, oxygen, nitrogen and hydrogen and a fill setting from 0 to 100. The first build adds 0.99 × fill × V of the selected gas, so a fresh tank reads 59.4 atm at full fill before any exchange, and Tank Content reads 0.99 of the litre volume. Air is split into nitrogen, oxygen and CO2 at that point. Custom tanks filled by the fluid spawner take a separate path; its tooltip says 60 atm.

sections.title: Saved contents and reset
sections.body:
Fluid and gas tanks share one serializer. It saves the fill-pending flag as spawner_pending and both compartments, contained_volume and contained_volume_secondary. Each compartment keeps vol_0 to vol_12, the 13 species amounts in the internal unit, plus vol_total, temp and rad. The geometric volume is not saved; it is recomputed from the definition without touching the amounts or temperature. A saved temperature is clamped to −273 … 100000 and a non-finite one becomes 0.

A separate reset zeroes both compartments' amounts and totals and sets fill pending again, so the next pending fill treats the tank as new. It leaves the temperature as it was. A new tank starts at 20 °C. The pending fill skips a tank whose fill-pending flag is 0, so a restored 0 keeps the restored contents through that call. A build reconstructs the pipe networks before it runs the pending fill, and the diesel and jet-fuel fill is a separate step with its own request gate. A restored 0 therefore keeps the contents unless a later reset sets fill pending again.

sections.title: Pressure limits
sections.body: No maximum safe pressure, rupture threshold or pressure damage rule was found. The pressure law has no limit, the tank update moves contents and sets its outputs without a pressure test, and the saved fields and the shipped definitions have no pressure limit. The 59.4 atm start and the 100000 temperature bound are not safety ratings. General vehicle damage code lies outside these checks, so they do not show that tanks cannot fail.

findings.label: Compartment pressure law
findings.detail: All 13 fluid indices (0 to 12) enter only as liquid sum L or gas sum G, with A = L + G. Pure gas reduces to P = 60 × A ÷ V at any volume. Pure liquid in a volume up to 8 (80 L), such as a pipe network of 4, also gives 60 × A ÷ V. Pure liquid above volume 8 gives max(0.5 × A ÷ V, 7.5 × (A − V + 8)): under 0.5 atm until less than 8 (80 L) of room is left, then 7.5 atm per amount (per 75 L) up to 60 at full. Temperature does not enter. Inference from the instruction sequence; degenerate states follow the original SSE arithmetic. Report: investigation/fluids-network.md. Inputs: native:stormworks64.exe:f9206d85c82f:0x1402eb460@0x1402eb471, native:stormworks64.exe:f9206d85c82f:0x1402eb460@0x1402eb4b6, native:stormworks64.exe:f9206d85c82f:0x1402eb500@0x1402eb51b, native:stormworks64.exe:f9206d85c82f:0x1402eb500@0x1402eb539, native:stormworks64.exe:f9206d85c82f:0x1402eb550@0x1402eb550.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Two ratios from a fixed list of eight; RPS B is pulled toward the ratio × RPS A, so for N:1 the A side is fast. Switching is immediate and needs power.

sections.title: Ratio orientation
sections.body: Both ratios are chosen from eight fixed options, not typed numbers: 1:-1, 1:1, 6:5, 3:2, 9:5, 2:1, 5:2 and 3:1. Each option is a multiplier q: -1, 1, 0.8333333, 0.6666667, 0.5555556, 0.5, 0.4 and 0.33333334. The gearbox stores q on its RPS A connection and 1 ÷ q on RPS B, and the shaft solver pulls RPS B toward q × RPS A. For an N:1 option RPS A is therefore the fast side: at 3:1 with RPS A at 30, RPS B is pulled toward 10. At 6:5 RPS A turns 6/5 as fast as RPS B. 1:-1 targets the same speed with the opposite sign.

sections.title: Coupling
sections.body:
RPS A and RPS B stay two separate shaft groups joined by a bridge. Each update every group first mixes its own parts: weight I = 1 + Σ F and speed v = (previous speed + Σ F × submitted speed) ÷ I, with F each part's submitted solver weight. The bridge then adds the other group's speed with path weight h = 0.95 × c, where c is the bridge fraction, 1 for an intact gearbox. A path from A adds sign(q) × v_A × I_A × h to B's numerator and I_A × h ÷ |q| to B's weight; paths with h at or below 0.001 add nothing. For two groups this gives B' = (I_B v_B + sign(q) I_A v_A h) ÷ (I_B + I_A h ÷ |q|) and A' = (I_A v_A + sign(q) I_B v_B h) ÷ (I_A + I_B h |q|).

Two groups already at the ratio stay there, so 0.95 weakens the coupling weight and is not a 95% power efficiency or a 5% speed loss. There is no slip threshold: under load the two sides settle where the weights balance. Example from rest, A with one part of weight 200 at 30 RPS (v_A 29.85, I_A 201) and B with one part of weight 100 at 0 RPS (I_B 101): one pass at 3:1 gives A 25.75 and B 8.459 RPS.

sections.title: Switching and power
sections.body: Gear Switch off applies Ratio Off and on applies Ratio On. When the selected q differs from the stored one by more than 0.001, both stored ratios are replaced in the same update, with no interpolation or delay, and the gearbox requests 0.001 electricity. This only happens while max(0, (300 - EMP count) ÷ 300) × charge fraction is above 0, or with infinite electricity. Without power the gearbox keeps its last ratio and stays coupled: the bridge fraction is set to 1 every update before the power test.

sections.title: Damage
sections.body: Any nonzero damage sets both bridge fractions to 0 every update, so a damaged gearbox or clutch disconnects its two sides. Gearboxes and clutches use the shared damage setter, which stores at most 50. The shared repair routine lowers damage by an amount its caller passes, never below 0, and at 0 the next update couples the two sides again.

sections.title: Size variants
sections.body: The 1x1, 3x3 and 5x5 gearboxes share the eight ratios, the bridge and the power gate. Their force_emitter_max_force values 200, 1200 and 5000 are copied to the RPS A connection at binding. The gearbox does not submit them as a solver weight and the decoded update and shaft solve compare that copy with nothing, so in those paths size does not change the coupling.

sections.title: Torque meter readings
sections.body: A torque meter's RPS output copies the group speed. Its Torque output is the group's effective solver weight I + D, not newton-metres, so meters on both sides of a gearbox or clutch do not measure the torque it transmits.

findings.label: Two groups across one bridge
findings.value: A' = (I_A v_A + sign(q) I_B v_B h) ÷ (I_A + I_B h |q|); B' = (I_B v_B + sign(q) I_A v_A h) ÷ (I_B + I_A h ÷ |q|)
findings.detail: h = 0.95 × c, and no exchange when h is at or below 0.001. A pair already at v_B = q × v_A stays there, so 0.95 weakens the coupling weight and is not a 95% power efficiency or a 5% speed loss. Loops, both ports on one group and graph rebuilds are outside this two-group form. Report: investigation/transmission.md. findings.label: Bridge worked example
findings.detail: Group A from rest with one part of weight 200 at 30 RPS: v_A = 6000 ÷ 201 = 29.85 RPS, I_A = 201. Group B from rest with one part of weight 100 at 0 RPS: v_B = 0, I_B = 101. One pass at 3:1 gives A 25.75 and B 8.459 RPS; at 1:-1, A 20.21 and B -19.52. A standalone clutch at input 0.5 (c = 1/64) at 1:1 gives A 29.63 and B 0.8565. Groups already at A 30 and B 10 with 3:1 stay at 30 and 10. Python doubles; the game uses binary32 and phased component submissions. Report: investigation/transmission.md. limitations: Shaft speed is RPS and the bridge weights are solver units. Open items shared by all transmission parts, including SI torque, losses and breakage, are listed under Transmission on the parts index.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Charge per update is electric_magnitude × force_emitter_max_force × 0.1 × |ω| × min(|ω| ÷ 560, 0.25), with ω the shaft speed in RPS. Output shows 60 times that, the internal charge per simulated second.

sections.title: How the update works
sections.body: The generator submits its previous speed and force_emitter_max_force to its shaft group and takes the group's speed ω back, in RPS. With k = min(|ω| ÷ 560, 0.25), it deposits Q = electric_magnitude × force_emitter_max_force × 0.1 × |ω| × k into the network pool and keeps (1 − k) of its speed; that loss is the load it puts on the shaft. Charge grows with the square of speed below 140 RPS and linearly above it. Output is 60 × Q. Component updates run 60 times per simulated second, so Output is the charge deposited per simulated second while RPS holds steady. Example: a small generator at 50 RPS deposits 0.2679 per update and shows Output 16.07.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: Per RPS removed, the small, medium and large generator deposit 0.06, 2.25 and 10.625. Divided by force_emitter_max_force that is 0.06, 0.075 and 0.085. The shaft group weights each part's speed by its force_emitter_max_force, so for the same force-weighted speed removal the large generator yields 1.4167 times and the medium 1.25 times what the small one does.

sections.title: Compared with motors and the alternator
sections.body: A motor driving a generator of the same size on one shaft group returns 0.5 (small), 0.6818 (medium) or 0.8095 (large) of the motor's charge for an equal force-weighted speed change. At equal |ω| × k the modular alternator's coefficient is 0.05 against the small generator's 0.06.

sections.title: Units
sections.body: Output has no unit label. It reads internal charge per simulated second, the unit battery capacity is counted in. The generator's own buffer of 0.1 per listed voxel is a source in the pool like a battery, so it takes its share of each deposit until it is full.

sections.title: Several bridges and loops
sections.body: When gearboxes or clutches join several shaft groups, each group passes its speed to every group it reaches once, along the first path in queue order, scaled by 0.95 × engagement per link. A loop whose ratios agree within 0.9 to 1.1 adds nothing more. A loop whose ratios disagree brakes every group that source reached: their bridge shares are cleared and the source's weight is added with no speed, so the result depends on group order. A link back into the same group at any ratio other than about 1 brakes that group; with nothing else attached it then publishes half its mixed speed each update (Transmission, inference from the decoded rule).

limitations: Static analysis only; Q is in the internal charge unit. A conversion of internal charge to joules or watts was not recovered.

The force-weighted comparisons hold within one shaft group. Across gearbox and clutch bridges, loops and links back into the same group, speeds combine by the traversal rule under Transmission. When connector changes rebuild the groups is an open item listed there.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: HUD Small draws 32×32 pixels and HUD Large 96×96. HUDs use the monitor component, with the same Touch Output channels.

sections.title: Resolution by size
sections.body:
The game sets width = 32 × (voxel_max.x - voxel_min.x + 1) and height = 32 × (voxel_max.z - voxel_min.z + 1) from the definition's block bounds. The same size comes back from screen.getWidth() and screen.getHeight() in onDraw and on Touch Output number channels 1 and 2.

Sizes in pixels: HUD Small 32×32, HUD Large 96×96.

HUDs have component type 43, the monitor type, so the same resolution routine and touch setter apply. Their definitions leave the Touch Output description empty; the channel layout below is the explanation.

The listed voxel count and monitor_border do not change the pixel grid. The graphics quality setting scales the render target by 1, 2 or 4 after the size is stored, so it leaves the Lua and touch grid alone.

sections.title: Touchscreen channels
sections.body:
Touch Output is a composite. Number channels 1 and 2 carry the width and height in pixels, 3 and 4 the X and Y of the first touch, and 5 and 6 the X and Y of the second. Boolean channels 1 and 2 are on while the first and second touch are pressed. Coordinates are whole pixels from the upper left, X to the right and Y down, accepted from 0 up to the width and height inclusive.

The screen tracks at most two touches at once and ignores a third. Releasing a touch clears only its flag and leaves its last X and Y on the channels, so check the flag before using a coordinate. The touch area is the screen face inset by monitor_border on each side, stretched over the pixel grid.

sections.title: Lua callbacks
sections.body: Read the channels with input.getNumber and input.getBool in onTick, which runs once per logic tick; screen functions do nothing there. Draw in onDraw, which runs whenever a monitor draws the script and can run several times when one script drives several monitors. Composite functions do nothing in onDraw. The shipped example reads number channels 3 and 4 and boolean channel 1 in onTick and draws the matching rectangle in onDraw.

sections.title: Wiring
sections.body: Feed Video Signal from a microcontroller or camera, connect Electric and turn Power Switch on. For a touchscreen, wire Touch Output to a composite input on the microcontroller that draws the screen and its video output back to Video Signal. While the screen is switched off, every Touch Output channel reads 0.

limitations: Resolution and touch layout come from static analysis of one build and its shipped definitions; the game was not run and no touch was tested in game.

Still open: a fixed refresh rate in Hz and the delay from a touch to the next drawn frame. onDraw follows monitor rendering rather than the 60-per-second component update, and the draw scheduling, culling and caching were outside this pass.
Still open: which player or input event takes each touch slot, and how HUD hits reach the touch setter.

families.summary: Heavy rotors on the shared force-emitter law with rotation_speed 1.5 and blade_efficiency 0.02; at 10 RPS they give 92.023 or 183.756 and 110.818 or 221.394 internal force per RPS depending on the air weight branch, before the application cap.

sections.title: Thrust and shaft load
sections.body:
Each update the part reads its published shaft speed and computes w = RPS × 0.9999, the effective pitch p = clamp(saved pitch + input, -1, 1) and the load b = (2 × w × rotation_speed × π × blade_physics_length × p × 0.75 + p × U) × blade_efficiency × B × 0.32, where U is the relative flow along the thrust axis and B the number of intact blades. With q = clamp(b × 0.5 ÷ K, -10, 10), multiplied by 10 when the hub is below the water surface, it removes w × (1 - 1 ÷ (1 + q²)) RPS from its own speed and pushes with T = 1500 × K × removed RPS × efficiency, signed by the pitch.

The saved pitch starts at force_emitter_default_pitch 1, so effective pitch is clamp(1 + Collective): Collective -1 gives zero load and zero thrust, and 0 or more gives full pitch 1. Pitch alone cannot reverse their push; reversing the shaft does.

sections.title: Sizes
sections.body:
Heavy Rotor: K 120 or 60, 92.023 or 183.756 per RPS; Heavy Large Rotor: K 200 or 100, 110.818 or 221.394 per RPS. Figures are raw internal force per input RPS at 10 published RPS, effective pitch 1, 4 intact blades and no inflow, before the application cap.

Air parts take one of two solver weights, K = F ÷ 1000 or F × B ÷ 8000, depending on a definition byte the decode could not tie to a resource field; each figure gives both, the first for F ÷ 1000.

sections.title: Cyclic and hinge
sections.body:
Roll and Pitch, clamped to -1 to 1, move the point where the force acts by -4 × input along local X and Z and tilt the force direction by 0.4 × input. This tips the vehicle; no blade-by-blade phase is modelled.

The rotor body turns on a physical hinge whose motor is on while the RPS port is connected. Its impulse limit is 1000 for every size, and its target speed follows the speed the rotor kept on the previous update × force_emitter_rotation_speed.

sections.title: Water and altitude
sections.body:
With the hub below the water surface the rotor pushes not at all in this update, while its load ratio q is multiplied by 10, so it brakes the shaft much harder. The tooltip's decreased force is this cut-off.

Thrust is multiplied by (1 - 2.2413793e-5 × y)^5.3595023 of the vehicle's altitude y: 1 at sea level, 0 above 40000.

limitations: Internal force units before the 100 × S application cap. Open items shared by every propeller and rotor are listed under Propulsion.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Large and huge rotors on the shared force-emitter law with efficiency 1.25; at 10 RPS they give 68.139 or 135.901 and 58.019 or 115.972 internal force per RPS depending on the air weight branch, before the application cap.

sections.title: Thrust and shaft load
sections.body:
Each update the part reads its published shaft speed and computes w = RPS × 0.9999, the effective pitch p = clamp(saved pitch + input, -1, 1) and the load b = (2 × w × rotation_speed × π × blade_physics_length × p × 0.75 + p × U) × blade_efficiency × B × 0.32, where U is the relative flow along the thrust axis and B the number of intact blades. With q = clamp(b × 0.5 ÷ K, -10, 10), multiplied by 10 when the hub is below the water surface, it removes w × (1 - 1 ÷ (1 + q²)) RPS from its own speed and pushes with T = 1500 × K × removed RPS × efficiency, signed by the pitch.

The saved pitch starts at force_emitter_default_pitch 1, so effective pitch is clamp(1 + Collective): Collective -1 gives zero load and zero thrust, and 0 or more gives full pitch 1. Pitch alone cannot reverse their push; reversing the shaft does.

sections.title: Sizes
sections.body:
Large Rotor: K 40 or 20, 68.139 or 135.901 per RPS; Huge Rotor: K 200 or 100, 58.019 or 115.972 per RPS. Figures are raw internal force per input RPS at 10 published RPS, effective pitch 1, 4 intact blades and no inflow, before the application cap.

Air parts take one of two solver weights, K = F ÷ 1000 or F × B ÷ 8000, depending on a definition byte the decode could not tie to a resource field; each figure gives both, the first for F ÷ 1000.

sections.title: Cyclic and hinge
sections.body:
Roll and Pitch, clamped to -1 to 1, move the point where the force acts by -4 × input along local X and Z and tilt the force direction by 0.4 × input. This tips the vehicle; no blade-by-blade phase is modelled.

The rotor body turns on a physical hinge whose motor is on while the RPS port is connected. Its impulse limit is 1000 for every size, and its target speed follows the speed the rotor kept on the previous update × force_emitter_rotation_speed.

sections.title: Water and altitude
sections.body:
With the hub below the water surface the rotor pushes not at all in this update, while its load ratio q is multiplied by 10, so it brakes the shaft much harder. The tooltip's decreased force is this cut-off.

Thrust is multiplied by (1 - 2.2413793e-5 × y)^5.3595023 of the vehicle's altitude y: 1 at sea level, 0 above 40000.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. families.summary: Shaft-driven pumps with bias 4 × |RPS| × pump_pressure (1 small, 9 standard); at equal pressure the small pump reaches the 400 L/s bound at 5 RPS and the standard one at 0.556 RPS.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: The impeller reads the speed of the shaft on its RPS port and pushes with bias 4 × |RPS| × pump_pressure. Spinning the shaft backward pushes the same way. Unlike the electric pumps it is two-way: backpressure can push fluid back through it, and at low flow it exchanges temperature between its two networks. The shaft port records a load request of 0.1 × pump_pressure; its torque unit was not established.

sections.title: Flow
sections.body: At equal pressure the move is at most min(bias, 20) ÷ 30 amount per update, 20 L/s per unit of bias up to 400 L/s. The small pump (pump_pressure 1) reaches that ceiling at 5 RPS and the standard one (9) at 0.556 RPS. These are bounds; backpressure, fill and other ports lower the real flow.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: They pump only while the shaft turns; compare variants with the Flow Rate output in L/s.

families.summary: An unpaired intake sets its outgoing pressure to 0.1 × forward speed × an altitude factor; the large intake also pushes along its axis above 5 RPS.

sections.title: Ram pressure
sections.body: Each update an intake that the shared grid lookup pairs with no other part replaces its outgoing pressure with 0.1 × v × A, after averaging with its neighbours. v is the signed speed along the intake's facing direction at its position, so flying faster raises the pressure and moving backward makes it negative. A = clamp(1 − 1.5 × h ÷ 40000, 0, 1), with h the body's height, falls to 0 at 26666.67.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: Only the large intake's tooltip mentions additional thrust from turbo fans. In the code the large intake's force_emitter_blade_physics_length of 1 passes a 0.75 gate that the small intake's 0.5 does not. Above 5 RPS the large intake then pushes along its axis with 2600 × (RPS − 5) × A in internal force units and loses (RPS − 5) × 0.1 ÷ 60 RPS per update.

sections.title: Water and damage
sections.body: With the vehicle_damage setting on, the intake's RPS is multiplied each update by clamp(max(1 − m, 0.01), 0, 1)^0.1, m being a source sample at the intake. Below the water surface it is also multiplied by 0.8, and an undamaged intake above 0.5 RPS first sends a damage request of 1 to the routine that spreads overspeed damage through the joined jet parts.

families.summary: Takes half of the incoming pressure, gains 0.0000375 × pressure RPS when undamaged and charges its Electric connection; the medium turbine also joins a shaft with weight 160.

sections.title: Pressure to RPS
sections.body: After averaging, a turbine passes on half of its incoming pressure and keeps the other half's effect as speed: r0 = r + 0.0000375 × p_in. A turbine with any damage gains nothing. A chamber overspeed is one source of that damage; repairing the turbine to 0 damage restores the gain.

sections.title: Electricity
sections.body: Generator fraction k = min(r0 ÷ 10000, 0.02), reaching 0.02 at 200 RPS. Each update the Electric connection receives |r0| × 0.025 × k charge and the turbine keeps (1 - k) × r0. At 20 RPS and incoming pressure 32000 that is 0.0011236 charge per update and a submitted speed of 21.155056 RPS. Both sizes use electric_magnitude 0.025.

sections.title: Shaft
sections.body: Only the medium turbine has the RPS power connection. It submits its speed with weight 160 to the shaft's weighted average and takes back max(shaft RPS, 0). An electric motor can therefore spin it up, and props or generators can load it. 160 is a solver weight, not a torque in N m.

findings.label: Overspeed effect on the engine
findings.value: turbines with any damage stop gaining pressure-driven RPS
findings.detail: The first overspeed of an undamaged chamber requests damage 1 and gives it to every jet part joined to it. A turbine with nonzero damage skips its pressure-to-RPS step (test at 0x140352fa7), so 1 is enough; more damage adds nothing to that effect, and the cap of 50 is not an efficiency scale. Existing speed and pressure are not cleared and the chamber still burns fuel and adds pressure. Repairing a turbine to 0 restores its gain; repairing only the chamber leaves the other parts' damage in place. Report: investigation/new-issues-a.md. limitations: Static decompilation of one build; the game was not run. Figures are for one part in one update. What an assembled engine settles at depends on its duct network; the Jet engines category lists that and the unit questions as open.
Pressure, temperature, charge and force are internal units, not pascals, degrees, watts or newtons. The shaft weight 160 is a solver weight, not a torque in N m.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Under water a keel pushes against sideways water speed with 40 × u × min(0.5 × M, 400) × w × 10, adds a fixed downward force of 1000 and pulls itself back toward vertical with a torque up to 800 × K × |sin θ|, K = min(S, 4 × definition mass).

sections.title: Water force
sections.body: While immersed, a keel pushes against its own sideways water speed: F = -40 × n × u × D × w × Q. n is the keel's side axis, u = clamp(sideways speed, -50, 50) m/s, D = min(0.5 × M, 400) with M the body mass, w the immersion and Q = clamp(60 × rudder_surface_area, 0.5, 10). Every keel has area 13, so Q = 10, and on a body of mass 800 or more the force is 160000 × w × u internal units. It is linear in speed, not quadratic. The water counts as still: no current is subtracted.

sections.title: Immersion
sections.body: w = clamp(2 × (0.25 - (y - surface)), 0, 1), y being the keel point's height and surface the sampled wave height there. w rises from 0 to 1 over the 0.5 m around the surface. At w = 0 the keel does nothing.

sections.title: Application limit
sections.body: Each keel force goes through the application helper with limit 100, so its size is capped at 100 × S. S is the summed adjusted mass of every body joined to this one by joints, free or locked, so all of them share one S; the Control surfaces category gives the rule and examples. A single body with no auxiliary masses has S equal to its mass M. With M = S = 10000 and w = 1 the water force is 16000 at 0.1 m/s sideways, 160000 at 1 m/s and 800000 at 5 m/s; at 10 m/s the raw 1600000 is capped to 1000000.

sections.title: Downward force
sections.body: A keel also queues a fixed world-down force of 1000 whenever it is immersed at all. It does not grow with keel size, body mass, depth or keel_force_factor. The shipped keel_mass_scale is also 1000, but this is a force: the body's mass and inertia do not change.

sections.title: Self-righting torque
sections.body: While the keel's down axis points at or below horizontal, two equal and opposite forces of 200 × K × w × |d + (0, 1, 0)| act 2 m either side of the keel origin along that axis. They cancel as forces and leave a torque of 800 × K × w × |sin θ| at heel θ from vertical, before the per-force cap (inferred from the two applications). K = min(S, 4 × definition mass): at most 2000, 4000 and 8000 for the small, medium and large keel, so the torque coefficient reaches 1600000, 3200000 and 6400000. At 30° heel with S = 10000 that is 800000, 1600000 and 3200000. Past horizontal the pair switches off rather than continuing the sine.

sections.title: Forward-speed memory
sections.body: The keel keeps a slow average z of the body's speed along its forward axis, z ← z + 0.002 × (u_f - z) each update, and pushes horizontally along that axis with 4 × K × (z - u_f) at the body centre. A sudden 1 m/s forward speed change gives 7984, 15968 or 31936 against it on the first update, fading with a time constant of about 8.325 s (inference). Steady sideways sliding does not produce it.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: All three sizes have rudder_surface_area 13, so the water force and the downward force are the same for the same body state. Definition mass 500, 1000 and 2000 changes only the self-righting and memory terms, and only once S exceeds 2000; below that K = S for every size. The keels list 29, 147 and 305 voxels. Geometry still changes the assembled mass, inertia and how deep the keel sits, but the 2 m lever of the self-righting pair is the same for all.

sections.title: Shipped tuning values
sections.body: general_debug.txt lists eight keel settings. The game's realtime loader reads every file in data/realtime_values/ and stores each line under its full name, so the keel lines are parsed even though the executable contains none of their names. The keel routine uses embedded constants instead: 200, 2, 100, 40, 1000, 0.002 and 4 equal the file's values, but the water force uses limit 100 where keel_lateral_max_acc_scale says 20. Editing the file is not shown to change keel behaviour.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: Sideways water resistance is what lets a sail push the hull forward in a crosswind or upwind, so pair keels with sail anchors. keel_force_factor (default 1) scales only the self-righting and memory forces.

findings.label: Sail Anchor · tooltip
findings.value: Draw a rope logic link between four Sail Anchors in a loop to form a sail. A sail will convert force from the wind to the direction of the sail facing. The sail force is strongest when fully facing the wind to act as a parachute, but also has a strong force when facing slightly off a right-angle from the wind to act as a wing. A keel is recommended for sailboats to apply sail forces in a useful direction.

findings.label: Cap scale S
findings.value: S = Σ adjusted body mass over the label group
findings.detail: For each body i the builder zeroes S_i in a parallel float list (0x1404bea4e) and adds +0x72c of every body j with the same label. Every body in a label group gets the same S. findings.label: Cap-scale group flood
findings.detail: Builds one integer label per vehicle body (assembly +0x18). For each component link it calls vtable slot +0x60, follows the counterpart at +0x150 or +0x148 to its body through component +0x28 and gives that body the same label. The flood does not test joint limits, the lock input, relative motion or motor power. Multibody joints (vtable 0x140b02a08) return themselves from slot +0x60 (0x1400cb6a0, mov rax,rcx; ret), so a pivot, hinge, piston or other multibody joint puts its two bodies in one label group, free or locked. Winches (vtable 0x140b958e8) also return themselves. The extractor re-reads these slot pointers. Report: investigation/force-cap.md. Function 0x1404c88e0-0x1404c8eab; instruction bytes ff5060 at 0x1404c8b21. Interpretation rests on retained output investigation/native/behavior/../force-cap/asm/locked-group-builder.asm:L169-L195; ../force-cap/pseudocode/0x1404c88e0.c. findings.label: Cap scale examples
findings.value: 1000; 1001 for 1000 + 1 on one joint; 992.727273 with an auxiliary mass of 1; 1000 and 1 when not joined
findings.detail: One body of mass 1000: S = 1000, so the caps are 5 × S = 5000, 100 × S = 100000 and 1000 × S = 1000000. Bodies of 1000 and 1 joined by a joint, free or locked: T = 1001, H = 1000, D = 1000 + 1000 ÷ 40 = 1025, r = 1001 ÷ 1025, adjusted masses 976.585366 and 24.414634, S = 1001 for both bodies and an air cap of 5 × S = 5005. One body of 1000 with one auxiliary mass of 1: D = 1000 + 1000 ÷ 120, S = 992.727273 and the adjusted auxiliary mass 8.272727, together 1001. Bodies of 1000 and 1 with no joint between them: S = 1000 and S = 1. The cap applies to each force separately, so it is not a budget for the whole vehicle. Calculations from the decoded arithmetic; no game measurement. Report: investigation/force-cap.md. families.summary: Same eight ratios, A-to-B orientation, bridge and power gate as the modular gearboxes; torque_gearbox_2's tooltip states a 4000 torque-difference limit.

sections.title: Ratio orientation
sections.body: Both ratios are chosen from eight fixed options, not typed numbers: 1:-1, 1:1, 6:5, 3:2, 9:5, 2:1, 5:2 and 3:1. Each option is a multiplier q: -1, 1, 0.8333333, 0.6666667, 0.5555556, 0.5, 0.4 and 0.33333334. The gearbox stores q on its RPS A connection and 1 ÷ q on RPS B, and the shaft solver pulls RPS B toward q × RPS A. For an N:1 option RPS A is therefore the fast side: at 3:1 with RPS A at 30, RPS B is pulled toward 10. At 6:5 RPS A turns 6/5 as fast as RPS B. 1:-1 targets the same speed with the opposite sign.

sections.title: Coupling
sections.body:
RPS A and RPS B stay two separate shaft groups joined by a bridge. Each update every group first mixes its own parts: weight I = 1 + Σ F and speed v = (previous speed + Σ F × submitted speed) ÷ I, with F each part's submitted solver weight. The bridge then adds the other group's speed with path weight h = 0.95 × c, where c is the bridge fraction, 1 for an intact gearbox. A path from A adds sign(q) × v_A × I_A × h to B's numerator and I_A × h ÷ |q| to B's weight; paths with h at or below 0.001 add nothing. For two groups this gives B' = (I_B v_B + sign(q) I_A v_A h) ÷ (I_B + I_A h ÷ |q|) and A' = (I_A v_A + sign(q) I_B v_B h) ÷ (I_A + I_B h |q|).

Two groups already at the ratio stay there, so 0.95 weakens the coupling weight and is not a 95% power efficiency or a 5% speed loss. There is no slip threshold: under load the two sides settle where the weights balance. Example from rest, A with one part of weight 200 at 30 RPS (v_A 29.85, I_A 201) and B with one part of weight 100 at 0 RPS (I_B 101): one pass at 3:1 gives A 25.75 and B 8.459 RPS.

sections.title: Switching and power
sections.body: Gear Switch off applies Ratio Off and on applies Ratio On. When the selected q differs from the stored one by more than 0.001, both stored ratios are replaced in the same update, with no interpolation or delay, and the gearbox requests 0.001 electricity. This only happens while max(0, (300 - EMP count) ÷ 300) × charge fraction is above 0, or with infinite electricity. Without power the gearbox keeps its last ratio and stays coupled: the bridge fraction is set to 1 every update before the power test.

sections.title: Damage
sections.body: Any nonzero damage sets both bridge fractions to 0 every update, so a damaged gearbox or clutch disconnects its two sides. Gearboxes and clutches use the shared damage setter, which stores at most 50. The shared repair routine lowers damage by an amount its caller passes, never below 0, and at 0 the next update couples the two sides again.

sections.title: Legacy definitions
sections.body: Both legacy definitions carry torque_component_type 1 and run the gearbox code above. Their force_emitter_max_force values, 1000 for torque_gearbox and 9999999 for torque_gearbox_2, are copied to the RPS A connection at binding and not submitted as a solver weight. Only torque_gearbox_2's tooltip states an operating limit of 4000 torque difference, without a unit. The gearbox update, ratio helper and shaft solve hold no 4000 and compare the copied value with nothing, so the limit is not enforced in those paths. Where it is enforced is an open item under Transmission on the parts index.

sections.title: Torque meter readings
sections.body: A torque meter's RPS output copies the group speed. Its Torque output is the group's effective solver weight I + D, not newton-metres, so meters on both sides of a gearbox or clutch do not measure the torque it transmits.

limitations: Shaft speed is RPS and the bridge weights are solver units. Open items shared by all transmission parts, including SI torque, losses and breakage, are listed under Transmission on the parts index.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Mixes two liquid compartments of 20 L (2x2) or 125 L (5x5) each, moving 0.03 of the gap per update weighted by the stored liquid amount on each side.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: Case 0x10 uses the liquid capacity helper for both sides: q is the stored amount of fresh water, diesel, jet fuel, oil, seawater, slurry and saturated slurry, each with weight 1, so fresh water and seawater count the same. Gas in a side counts 0. Each side passes fluid only with both its In and Out ports connected.

sections.title: Performance drivers
sections.body: Per update the hotter compartment loses and the colder gains in proportion 0.03 × q_other ÷ (qA + qB), conserving qA × TA + qB × TB. Without through-flow the gap keeps 0.161 of its size after one simulated second (time constant 0.547 s). With flow, arriving liquid is mixed by the side's amount after the move, and the Out port carries the side's mixed temperature.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: Each side holds V = 0.5 × listed voxels: 2 units (20 L) for the 2x2 with 4 voxels and 12.5 units (125 L) for the 5x5 with 25. At equal fill the 5x5 has 6.25 times the q on each side. The gap still shrinks by the same 0.03 fraction per update.

sections.title: Equal-flow comparison
sections.body: At 60 L/s on each side, 0.8 fill, inlets of 100 and 20 °C and ambient 20 °C, the 2x2 emits 85.54 and 33.13 °C and the 5x5 66.02 and 46.64 °C. Temp A and Temp B read 84.68 and 33.90 °C for the 2x2, 65.68 and 46.90 °C for the 5x5. The hot side drops by 18.1 % and 42.5 % of the inlet gap; these figures include ambient loss and the game's mixing rule, so they are not a conserved-energy effectiveness. These are outputs of the report's 60 Hz model with fixed boundary networks and a prescribed flow, not game measurements or a pump rating. The interactive graph below runs the same model.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Temp A and Temp B read the stored compartment temperatures in °C after this update's exchange and ambient step. Fluid leaving the Out ports was emitted earlier in the same update, so its temperature can differ. Both compartments also drift toward the surrounding temperature by 0.001 per update, so an idle exchanger slowly settles to ambient: the leak alone has a time constant of 16.7 simulated seconds.

findings.label: Exchanger capacity q
findings.value: pure gas q = P × V ÷ 60; liquid q = stored liquid amount
findings.detail: q is the side's stored amount of its phase in native units, 10 L of liquid or 600 L of expanded gas per amount. Inference from the pressure law: pure gas has P = 60 × G ÷ V, so q = G = P × V ÷ 60 and doubling pressure doubles q at a fixed volume. At equal volume a 1 atm gas side has V ÷ 60 and a full liquid side V; at 60 atm the gas side equals the full liquid side. With gas and liquid in one side, sum the gas amounts instead of using P × V ÷ 60. Wrong-phase contents give 0 toward that side's q but still move through the ports. Report: investigation/heat-exchangers.md. findings.label: Recipient amount in temperature mixing

families.summary: Fixed-pitch underwater propellers with solver weight K = F ÷ 1000 (20, 100 and 200). They push only with the hub at or below the water surface; at 10 RPS in still water the raw internal force is 2220.143, 7298.928 and 10290.409 per RPS before the application cap.

sections.title: How thrust follows RPS
sections.body:
Each update the part reads its published shaft speed and computes w = RPS × 0.9999, the effective pitch p = clamp(saved pitch + input, -1, 1) and the load b = (2 × w × rotation_speed × π × blade_physics_length × p × 0.75 + p × U) × blade_efficiency × B × 0.32, where U is the relative flow along the thrust axis and B the number of intact blades. With q = clamp(b × 0.5 ÷ K, -10, 10), multiplied by 10 when the hub is below the water surface, it removes w × (1 - 1 ÷ (1 + q²)) RPS from its own speed and pushes with T = 1500 × K × removed RPS × efficiency, signed by the pitch.

The pitch is fixed at force_emitter_default_pitch 1 and the part has no pitch input, so turning the shaft backwards reverses the push. Thrust grows about with RPS cubed at low speed and close to linearly at high speed.

sections.title: Sizes
sections.body:
Small Propeller: K 20, 2220.143 per RPS, 0.7400 RPS removed; Large Propeller: K 100, 7298.928 per RPS, 0.4866 RPS removed; Giant Propeller: K 200, 10290.409 per RPS, 0.3430 RPS removed. Figures are raw internal force per input RPS at 10 published RPS, effective pitch 1, 4 intact blades and no inflow, before the application cap.

F rises 1 : 5 : 10 across the sizes, but the figures rise far less, because a larger F raises K and lowers the load ratio. The small propeller takes the most speed off its shaft per update.

sections.title: Water and flow
sections.body: The hub must be at or below the sampled water surface; above it the propeller pushes not at all but still loads its shaft. Under water its load ratio q is multiplied by 10. The flow term U is minus the hub's velocity through still water, projected on the thrust axis and signed by the pitch: positive U adds to the load and negative U takes from it. Water currents are not subtracted.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: The giant propeller turns its rotation_speed of 0.5 and blade_efficiency of 0.25 into the highest force per RPS, at the lowest speed loss per RPS of the three.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Clutch Pressure is clamped to 0 to 1 and cubed; engagement follows that target by at most 0.1 per update and sets how far crank and output speeds pull together.

sections.title: Engagement
sections.body: The target is u³, with u the Clutch Pressure clamped to 0 to 1, so 0.5 asks for 0.125. Stored engagement moves toward the target by at most 0.1 per update: from 0 at input 0.5 it reads 0.1, then 0.125. A full engage or release takes at least ten updates, 0.167 simulated seconds.

sections.title: Output
sections.body: Each update the clutch gives its output shaft group the weight engagement × I and the crank RPS, then moves the crank RPS toward the output group's speed by the engagement. At engagement 1 the crank takes the output's speed. Clutches are not part of the crank weight sum, and the clutch weight is a solver weight, not a torque in N m.

sections.title: Standalone clutch
sections.body: The standalone clutch part runs different code. It sets its coupling directly to e × clamp(input, 0, 1)^6 each update with no slew, so input 0.5 gives 1/64 there against a target of 0.125 here, and it joins two shaft groups through the 0.95 bridge rather than a crank.

findings.label: Clutch coupling examples
findings.value: input 0.5 → c = 1/64; no coupling below input 0.3189
findings.detail: At full availability c = u⁶: input 0.5 gives 0.015625 = 1/64 and input 1 gives 1. The path weight 0.95 × c must exceed 0.001, so with an isolated clutch input below (0.001 ÷ 0.95)^(1/6) = 0.3189 transfers nothing. That threshold comes from the solver's path cutoff, not from a clamp on the input. The modular clutch instead targets u³ and moves by at most 0.1 per update. Report: investigation/transmission.md. families.summary: Crank parts share one RPS state. The crank group starts at inertia 1 and each crankshaft adds 0.7, 8, 15 or 25.

sections.title: Crank group
sections.body: The crank walk joins parts through couplings named crankshaft, crankshaft_3, crankshaft_5, belt and cylinder, so a crankshaft, its cylinders, converters, belts and flywheels form one group with one RPS value. The group starts at I = 1 and F = 0; crankshafts add 0.7 (1x1), 8 (3x1), 15 (3x3) and 25 (5x5) to I and 0 to F. Their own component update does nothing, so the crankshaft changes no speed by itself.

sections.title: Performance drivers
sections.body: Each update the crank keeps r × (1 - 0.01 × (1 - F ÷ I)) of its speed, 0.99 without a flywheel, and every cylinder impulse divides by I, so heavier assemblies respond more slowly to each combustion impulse. Cylinders read the shared crank speed for their intake, efficiency and 60 RPS cut-off.

families.summary: Joins two crankshaft sizes into one crank group at a 1:1 speed and adds inertia 8 (Converter 3 to 1) or 15 (Converter 5 to 3).

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The crank walk follows a converter's crankshaft couplings like any other, so both sides end up in the same group and read the same RPS. Its component update (types 20 and 24) does nothing, so there is no speed ratio and no torque multiplication. The size names describe the couplings. The converter adds its engine_max_force, 8 or 15, to the crank inertia I and 0 to the frictionless sum, as it has no engine_frictionless_force attribute.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Each undamaged cylinder above 2 RPS adds 80000 × burned fuel × efficiency ÷ I RPS per update. Best efficiency at air:fuel ratio 13.6 + 0.4t, 13.68 at 20 °C; no fuel above 60 RPS.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: A cylinder adds speed only when the crank is above 2 RPS, its air:fuel ratio is inside the window 12 − 2t … 16 + 4t (t = manifold °C ÷ 100, clamped 0…1), the crank is at or below 60 RPS and its damage is below 20. Fuel is capped by the diesel available in its fuel manifolds and intake by the oxygen in its air manifolds.

sections.title: Speed impulse
sections.body: Δr = gain × burned fuel × efficiency ÷ I, added straight to the crank RPS, with I = 1 + Σ engine_max_force of the crank group. Gain is 80000 at damage 0 and 40000 at damage 1 to 19. Burned fuel is the fuel term times the exhaust share, so with ideal supply one cylinder adds 0.32 × r × voxels × throttle × efficiency ÷ I per update, or 19.2 × voxels × throttle × efficiency ÷ I per revolution at a held speed. Cylinders run one after another and each sees the speed the earlier ones left. This is an RPS step, not a torque in N m, and there is no separate firing stroke.

sections.title: Performance drivers
sections.body: Fuel per update = RPS × 4e-6 × listed voxels × fuel throttle, which is RPS × 0.00024 × listed voxels × fuel throttle per simulated second. Intake = RPS × 2.8e-6 × listed voxels ÷ 60 × air throttle × pressure factor, where the pressure factor rises from 1 to 2 with air-manifold pressure in atmospheres (scale 0.01). The air:fuel ratio is 600 × admitted oxygen ÷ max(admitted diesel, 1e-08). Efficiency = speed efficiency × mixture factor; speed efficiency = clamp(4(0.02·RPS + 0.5)/(0.02·RPS + 1)² − 1, 0, 1), and the mixture factor 1 − 2(s − 0.6)² peaks at the air:fuel ratio 13.6 cold, 14.0 hot. The displayed Stoichiometric value is 2s − 1, so aim for about 0.2.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: The cylinder code multiplies fuel and intake by the definition's listed voxel count: 1 for the 1x1, 27 for the 3x3 and 125 for the 5x5. At equal RPS and throttle a 3x3 cylinder therefore admits 27 times the fuel of a 1x1 and heats its manifolds correspondingly. Their inertia weights are 0.6, 12 and 15, and each adds 40 × its voxels to the manifold heat capacity.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: With equal air and fuel throttles and no boost the ratio is 7, below the window, so the engine will not fire; reduce fuel throttle to roughly half of air throttle or add manifold pressure. Exhaust that cannot fit into the exhaust manifolds reduces the speed impulse and heat in proportion (Exhaust % in the inspection text). Above 115 °C with overheating enabled the cylinder takes 1 damage at once and 1 more every 300 updates, once per 5 simulated seconds; with damage 1 to 19 its gain halves from 80000 to 40000, and from 20 it adds no speed. Damage is the component's saved damage field, capped at 50 by the setter.

sections.title: Composite telemetry
sections.body: Composite Data number 1 (Air Volume) is 6000 × admitted oxygen, number 2 (Fuel Volume) is 10 × admitted diesel, in litres, and number 3 is the manifold temperature in °C after this cylinder's heat. Numbers 1 and 2 are per cylinder visit, not per second, and number 1 ÷ number 2 is the air:fuel ratio when fuel is nonzero. Both stay nonzero outside the combustion window, so they show demand, not combustion. Number 1 is not the air stored in the manifold.

findings.label: Crank RPS after one update from 20 RPS
findings.value: 1 cylinder, I = 2.3: 22.1114; 4 cylinders, I = 4.1: 25.343; 4 cylinders and a 1x1 flywheel, I = 154.1: 20.1339
findings.detail: 1x1 cylinders on one 1x1 crankshaft at 20 °C, mixture at its peak AFR 13.68, full fuel throttle, ideal supply and exhaust room, damage 0. limitations: Reconstructed from static decompilation; signs and offsets were checked against instruction bytes, but no in-game run confirmed the curves.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Joins the crank group and carries crank RPS 1:1 to starters, alternators and fluid pumps; adds inertia 0.6, or 5 for the power manifolds.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The drive belt has one crankshaft coupling and four belt couplings. The crank walk follows both kinds, so the belt is part of the crank group. Its component update (type 4, and 17 and 23 for the power manifolds) does nothing: no ratio, slip or loss. It adds 0.6 (drive belt) or 5 (3x3 and 5x5 power manifolds) to the crank inertia I and 0 to the frictionless sum.

sections.title: Accessories
sections.body: A starter, alternator or fluid pump on the belt keeps its own speed w in RPS, in the crank's reference. Each update it mixes with the crank by its Clutch Pressure u, clamped to 0 to 1 and used linearly: r becomes r + J ÷ (I + J) × u × (w - r) and w becomes w + I ÷ (I + J) × u × (r - w), with J = 0.5 the accessory's own weight. I × r + J × w is unchanged and at u = 1 both end at the same speed. The alternator then applies its speed drag; the pump and starter keep 0.99 of their speed.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Exhaust space limits combustion: the share that fits sets both the speed impulse and heat. The manifold drains through the port exchange with an outward bias of 10.

sections.title: Performance drivers
sections.body: The cylinder computes produced exhaust as fuel × 20 ÷ 60 and the share that fits into the exhaust manifold network; the speed impulse and manifold heating are multiplied by that share, shown as Exhaust %.

sections.title: Outflow
sections.body: Each exhaust manifold holds a compartment of 1/3 amount, 3.33 L, which reads 60 atm when full. Each update its Exhaust port runs the same port exchange as tanks and radiators, with bias 10 and factor 1: exhaust leaves for the pipe network while the manifold pressure is above the network's minus 10, and comes back only when the network is more than 10 above. The move each update is at most half the new demand and follows the network's allocation from the update before, limited by what the source holds, the room on the other side and 1 amount per update into the pipe. Delivered flow therefore depends on the connected network and the other ports on it; there is no fixed exhaust rate.

findings.label: Compartment pressure law
findings.detail: All 13 fluid indices (0 to 12) enter only as liquid sum L or gas sum G, with A = L + G. Pure gas reduces to P = 60 × A ÷ V at any volume. Pure liquid in a volume up to 8 (80 L), such as a pipe network of 4, also gives 60 × A ÷ V. Pure liquid above volume 8 gives max(0.5 × A ÷ V, 7.5 × (A − V + 8)): under 0.5 atm until less than 8 (80 L) of room is left, then 7.5 atm per amount (per 75 L) up to 60 at full. Temperature does not enter. Inference from the instruction sequence; degenerate states follow the original SSE arithmetic. Report: investigation/fluids-network.md. Inputs: native:stormworks64.exe:f9206d85c82f:0x1402eb460@0x1402eb471, native:stormworks64.exe:f9206d85c82f:0x1402eb460@0x1402eb4b6, native:stormworks64.exe:f9206d85c82f:0x1402eb500@0x1402eb51b, native:stormworks64.exe:f9206d85c82f:0x1402eb500@0x1402eb539, native:stormworks64.exe:f9206d85c82f:0x1402eb550@0x1402eb550.

families.summary: Adds 150, 600 or 2400 to both the crank inertia I and the frictionless sum F, so each impulse is smaller and the crank loses less speed per update.

sections.title: Performance drivers
sections.body: Each update the crank keeps 1 - 0.01 × (1 - F ÷ I) of its speed before the cylinders run, and every cylinder impulse divides by I. Flywheels are the only shipped parts with a nonzero F, equal to their inertia weight. Example from 20 RPS at full throttle: four 1x1 cylinders on a 1x1 crankshaft (I = 4.1) reach 25.343 RPS after one update; with a 1x1 flywheel (I = 154.1, F = 150) they reach 20.1339 RPS, and coasting keeps 0.999734 per update instead of 0.99.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The starter's coupling weights its own inertia (engine_max_force 0.5) against the crank inertia and only assists below 5 RPS, so a large flywheel noticeably lengthens cranking. Expect smaller RPS dips under load in exchange.

families.summary: Manifold extensions carry the shared manifold group between cylinders and manifolds; they add no crank inertia and no heat capacity.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The manifold walk joins parts through couplings named manifold, so cylinders, manifolds and extensions connected this way share one manifold group: one temperature, one heat capacity, one pair of throttles and the same air, fuel, exhaust and coolant manifolds. In the registration switch cylinders add 40 × their voxels to the heat capacity, while extensions (types 13, 14 and 15) add nothing. Their component update does nothing and they are outside the crank weight mask.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Monitors draw 32 pixels per block of width and height, from 32×32 (Monitor 1x1) to 288×160 (Monitor 9x5). Touch Output reports that size and two touch points in pixels.

sections.title: Resolution by size
sections.body:
The game sets width = 32 × (voxel_max.x - voxel_min.x + 1) and height = 32 × (voxel_max.z - voxel_min.z + 1) from the definition's block bounds. The same size comes back from screen.getWidth() and screen.getHeight() in onDraw and on Touch Output number channels 1 and 2.

Sizes in pixels: Monitor 1x1 32×32, Monitor 1x2 64×32, Monitor 1x3 96×32, Monitor 2x2 64×64, Monitor 2x3 96×64, Monitor 3x3 96×96, Monitor 5x3 160×96, Monitor 9x5 288×160.

Follow the bounds, not the name: in Monitor 1x2, 1x3 and 2x3 the first number is the height in blocks, while 5x3 and 9x5 give the width first.

The listed voxel count and monitor_border do not change the pixel grid. The graphics quality setting scales the render target by 1, 2 or 4 after the size is stored, so it leaves the Lua and touch grid alone.

sections.title: Touchscreen channels
sections.body:
Touch Output is a composite. Number channels 1 and 2 carry the width and height in pixels, 3 and 4 the X and Y of the first touch, and 5 and 6 the X and Y of the second. Boolean channels 1 and 2 are on while the first and second touch are pressed. Coordinates are whole pixels from the upper left, X to the right and Y down, accepted from 0 up to the width and height inclusive.

The screen tracks at most two touches at once and ignores a third. Releasing a touch clears only its flag and leaves its last X and Y on the channels, so check the flag before using a coordinate. The touch area is the screen face inset by monitor_border on each side, stretched over the pixel grid.

sections.title: Lua callbacks
sections.body: Read the channels with input.getNumber and input.getBool in onTick, which runs once per logic tick; screen functions do nothing there. Draw in onDraw, which runs whenever a monitor draws the script and can run several times when one script drives several monitors. Composite functions do nothing in onDraw. The shipped example reads number channels 3 and 4 and boolean channel 1 in onTick and draws the matching rectangle in onDraw.

sections.title: Wiring
sections.body: Feed Video Signal from a microcontroller or camera, connect Electric and turn Power Switch on. For a touchscreen, wire Touch Output to a composite input on the microcontroller that draws the screen and its video output back to Video Signal. While the screen is switched off, every Touch Output channel reads 0.

findings.label: Touch slots
findings.detail: Two 12-byte slots start at component+0x148 and +0x154. The setter first matches a slot holding the same integer point, otherwise a press takes the first slot whose pressed byte is clear. Both loops stop at 2, so a third simultaneous touch is ignored. families.summary: Aircraft propeller on the shared force-emitter law with rotation_speed 3; at 10 RPS it gives 109.488 or 218.296 internal force per RPS by air weight branch, before the application cap.

sections.title: Thrust and shaft load
sections.body:
Each update the part reads its published shaft speed and computes w = RPS × 0.9999, the effective pitch p = clamp(saved pitch + input, -1, 1) and the load b = (2 × w × rotation_speed × π × blade_physics_length × p × 0.75 + p × U) × blade_efficiency × B × 0.32, where U is the relative flow along the thrust axis and B the number of intact blades. With q = clamp(b × 0.5 ÷ K, -10, 10), multiplied by 10 when the hub is below the water surface, it removes w × (1 - 1 ÷ (1 + q²)) RPS from its own speed and pushes with T = 1500 × K × removed RPS × efficiency, signed by the pitch.

Collective drives the pitch input. The saved pitch starts at 1, so Collective -1 gives zero thrust and 0 or more gives full pitch 1; it cannot reverse the push. The tooltip's torque wording describes the shaft load: every RPS the propeller removes from its shaft becomes 1500 × K internal force.

sections.title: Figures
sections.body:
Aircraft Propeller: K 70 or 35, 109.488 or 218.296 per RPS. Figures are raw internal force per input RPS at 10 published RPS, effective pitch 1, 4 intact blades and no inflow, before the application cap.

Air parts take one of two solver weights, K = F ÷ 1000 or F × B ÷ 8000, depending on a definition byte the decode could not tie to a resource field; each figure gives both, the first for F ÷ 1000.

sections.title: Water and altitude
sections.body: With the hub below the water surface it pushes not at all and its load ratio is multiplied by 10. Thrust is multiplied by (1 - 2.2413793e-5 × y)^5.3595023 of the vehicle's altitude y: 1 at sea level, 0 above 40000.

families.summary: Outputs the part's world height above the fixed sea-level datum y = 0, in metres: not clearance over terrain or the local wave surface.

sections.title: Reading
sections.body:
Logic case 18 moves the part's position through the body's world transform and outputs the world Y coordinate. It reads no terrain, seabed, wave or pressure value and keeps no previous position, so the output is height above y = 0, the sea level the tooltip names, whatever lies below the part. Over land it does not show height above the ground, and over water it does not measure from the local wave surface.

The output is 0 when the height is above 40000 or the world X coordinate is above 156000. Both tests are one-sided.

sections.title: Timing
sections.body: There is no sensor timer, history or smoothing. The value is recomputed on every logic update, 60 per simulated second, and written only when it changes.
