families.summary: Underwater thruster on the marine force-emitter law with K = F ÷ 1000 = 40; 4440.285 internal force per RPS at 10 RPS in still water, before the application cap. Mount it on a robotic pivot to steer the push.

sections.title: Thrust and shaft load
sections.body:
Each update the part reads its published shaft speed and computes w = RPS × 0.9999, the effective pitch p = clamp(saved pitch + input, -1, 1) and the load b = (2 × w × rotation_speed × π × blade_physics_length × p × 0.75 + p × U) × blade_efficiency × B × 0.32, where U is the relative flow along the thrust axis and B the number of intact blades. With q = clamp(b × 0.5 ÷ K, -10, 10), multiplied by 10 when the hub is below the water surface, it removes w × (1 - 1 ÷ (1 + q²)) RPS from its own speed and pushes with T = 1500 × K × removed RPS × efficiency, signed by the pitch.

Pitch is fixed at 1, so reversing the shaft reverses the push. It pushes only with the hub at or below the water surface, and under water its load ratio q is multiplied by 10.

sections.title: Figures
sections.body:
Azimuth Thruster: K 40, 4440.285 per RPS, 0.7400 RPS removed. Figures are raw internal force per input RPS at 10 published RPS, effective pitch 1, 4 intact blades and no inflow, before the application cap.

It removes the same speed per RPS as the small marine propeller: with the same blade_physics_length 0.25, twice the blade_efficiency (0.15) and twice the F (40000), its load and K both double and q is unchanged. Each removed RPS therefore pushes twice as hard.

families.summary: Attaches to another Electric Connector whose centre is under 0.5 m away, with a point-to-point joint and no magnetic pull; Release detaches it and blocks reattaching for 120 updates.

sections.title: Attaching and release
sections.body: It looks for another Electric Connector within 10 m and attaches when the centres are under 0.5 m apart, with no orientation test. Its definition flag 0x100000 turns the magnetic pull off, so the parts must be brought that close. A Bullet point-to-point joint then pins the centres together and leaves the parts free to turn; its break threshold is the largest double, so the joint has no finite holding limit. Release starts a 120-update count, 2 simulated seconds. While it runs the connector cannot attach and the scene pass detaches it. Holding Release keeps restarting the count, so it can attach again 120 updates after the input goes off.

sections.title: Transfers
sections.body: While linked, the two connectors' electric nodes point at each other, so the electrical pool builder treats both networks as one charge pool. The pool walk adds no capacity or loss for this link; battery output and consumer limits still apply. While linked, each update copies the composite signal, 32 on/off channels and 32 numbers, straight into the partner's Composite Data Receive and hands its video source to the partner's Video Data Receive. The copy has no buffer, scaling or averaging.

limitations: Conversion of the pull, body weight and joint impulse to newtons and kilograms, signal and video timing across a link, the electrical link of small, hinge and large connectors, the Mag All's contact filtering and what ordnance does after Launch are listed as open items in the Magnetic connectors, transfers and hardpoints mechanics article.
Static analysis of one build. Forces and impulses are in the game's internal units; no attachment, pull or break was measured in a running game.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Holds a hardpoint attachment on a fixed joint once their centres are under 0.5 m apart and line up. Release or Launch detaches it and blocks reattaching for 120 updates; Ordinance Type reads the attachment's code from 1 to 12.

sections.title: Attaching
sections.body: A body pairs only with an attachment, round or square, and an attachment only with a body. They attach when the centres are under 0.5 m apart and both axial samples, 0.25 m either side of the centre, lie within 0.1118 m of the partner's samples. There is no magnetic pull, so the parts must be placed that close. A Bullet fixed joint then locks position and rotation; its break threshold is the largest double, so the joint has no finite holding limit.

sections.title: Release and Launch
sections.body: Release and Launch both start a 120-update count, 2 simulated seconds, during which the body cannot attach and the scene pass detaches it. Holding either input keeps restarting the count. Launch also sets a latch on the attached part, which that part outputs as Launched. The latch stays on after the parts separate until the component is reset. The Launch branch calls no firing, ignition, projectile or extra force routine, so anything the ordnance does after Launch has to come from its own logic reading Launched (inference from that branch).

sections.title: Ordnance type codes
sections.body:
While attached, the body's Ordinance Type output carries the attachment's selected code as a number, copied each update. The codes are the editor's hardpoint classes, not the weapon ammunition types:

- 1: Utility
- 2: Fuel
- 3: Unguided bomb
- 4: Laser Guided Bomb
- 5: GPS Guided Bomb
- 6: Rocket
- 7: Rocket Pod
- 8: Laser Guided Missile
- 9: GPS Guided Missile
- 10: Radar Guided Missile
- 11: Torpedo
- 12: Cannon

sections.title: Transfers
sections.body: Each side's electric node points at the other's, so both networks form one charge pool, with no capacity or loss for this link. The Fluid ports exchange with factor 0.5 and bias 0 in both directions; the networks stay separate. While linked, each update copies the composite signal, 32 on/off channels and 32 numbers, straight into the partner's Composite Data Receive and hands its video source to the partner's Video Data Receive. The copy has no buffer, scaling or averaging.

Static analysis of one build. Forces and impulses are in the game's internal units; no attachment, pull or break was measured in a running game.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Hangs from a Hardpoint Connector Body on a fixed joint once their centres are under 0.5 m apart and line up, sends its ordnance type code, 1 to 12, to the body, and outputs Launched after the body's Launch.

sections.title: Attaching
sections.body: A body pairs only with an attachment, round or square, and an attachment only with a body. They attach when the centres are under 0.5 m apart and both axial samples, 0.25 m either side of the centre, lie within 0.1118 m of the partner's samples. There is no magnetic pull, so the parts must be placed that close. A Bullet fixed joint then locks position and rotation; its break threshold is the largest double, so the joint has no finite holding limit.

sections.title: Ordnance type and Launched
sections.body:
Its ordnance type property defaults to 1. While attached it sends the code, as a number, to the body's Ordinance Type output each update. The codes are the editor's hardpoint classes, not the weapon ammunition types:

- 1: Utility
- 2: Fuel
- 3: Unguided bomb
- 4: Laser Guided Bomb
- 5: GPS Guided Bomb
- 6: Rocket
- 7: Rocket Pod
- 8: Laser Guided Missile
- 9: GPS Guided Missile
- 10: Radar Guided Missile
- 11: Torpedo
- 12: Cannon

When the body's Launch goes on, this part's latch is set and Launched turns on. The body then detaches and cannot attach again until 120 updates, 2 simulated seconds, after Launch goes off. Launched stays on after the parts separate until the component is reset. The Launch branch fires, ignites and pushes nothing itself (inference: wire Launched to this vehicle's own engines, rockets or warheads).

sections.title: Transfers
sections.body: Each side's electric node points at the other's, so both networks form one charge pool, with no capacity or loss for this link. The Fluid ports exchange with factor 0.5 and bias 0 in both directions; the networks stay separate. While linked, each update copies the composite signal, 32 on/off channels and 32 numbers, straight into the partner's Composite Data Receive and hands its video source to the partner's Video Data Receive. The copy has no buffer, scaling or averaging.

limitations: Conversion of the pull, body weight and joint impulse to newtons and kilograms, signal and video timing across a link, the electrical link of small, hinge and large connectors, the Mag All's contact filtering and what ordnance does after Launch are listed as open items in the Magnetic connectors, transfers and hardpoints mechanics article.
Static analysis of one build. Forces and impulses are in the game's internal units; no attachment, pull or break was measured in a running game.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Hangs from a Hardpoint Connector Body on a fixed joint once their centres are under 0.5 m apart and line up, sends its ordnance type code, 1 to 12, to the body, and outputs Launched after the body's Launch.

sections.title: Attaching
sections.body: A body pairs only with an attachment, round or square, and an attachment only with a body. They attach when the centres are under 0.5 m apart and both axial samples, 0.25 m either side of the centre, lie within 0.1118 m of the partner's samples. There is no magnetic pull, so the parts must be placed that close. A Bullet fixed joint then locks position and rotation; its break threshold is the largest double, so the joint has no finite holding limit.

sections.title: Ordnance type and Launched
sections.body:
Its ordnance type property defaults to 1. While attached it sends the code, as a number, to the body's Ordinance Type output each update. The codes are the editor's hardpoint classes, not the weapon ammunition types:

- 1: Utility
- 2: Fuel
- 3: Unguided bomb
- 4: Laser Guided Bomb
- 5: GPS Guided Bomb
- 6: Rocket
- 7: Rocket Pod
- 8: Laser Guided Missile
- 9: GPS Guided Missile
- 10: Radar Guided Missile
- 11: Torpedo
- 12: Cannon

When the body's Launch goes on, this part's latch is set and Launched turns on. The body then detaches and cannot attach again until 120 updates, 2 simulated seconds, after Launch goes off. Launched stays on after the parts separate until the component is reset. The Launch branch fires, ignites and pushes nothing itself (inference: wire Launched to this vehicle's own engines, rockets or warheads).

sections.title: Transfers
sections.body: Each side's electric node points at the other's, so both networks form one charge pool, with no capacity or loss for this link. The Fluid ports exchange with factor 0.5 and bias 0 in both directions; the networks stay separate. While linked, each update copies the composite signal, 32 on/off channels and 32 numbers, straight into the partner's Composite Data Receive and hands its video source to the partner's Video Data Receive. The copy has no buffer, scaling or averaging.

Static analysis of one build. Forces and impulses are in the game's internal units; no attachment, pull or break was measured in a running game.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Attaches to another Hinge Connector whose centre is under 0.25 m away and whose samples line up, then holds with a hinge joint. magnet_force 0.15 scales only the pull before attaching.

sections.title: Attaching
sections.body: It looks for another Hinge Connector within 10 m. It attaches when the two centres are under 0.25 m apart and both of its endpoint samples, 0.25 m either side of the centre along the hinge axis, lie within 0.1118 m of an endpoint sample on the other connector. With coincident centres that allows the axes to differ by up to 25.8 degrees; turning about the axis moves neither sample (inference from the sample geometry). Both connectors need Magnet Toggle on, usable electricity, no existing link and different bodies.

sections.title: Pull before attaching
sections.body: Until it attaches, each update pulls toward the partner with F = 60 × 0.15 × P × W × d ÷ (1 + |d|²) for the offset d between matching samples, and nothing once |d| reaches 1 m. P is 1 with infinite electricity and otherwise max(0, (300 - EMP) ÷ 300) × charge fraction. W is the smaller of the two bodies' native weight field, or the larger when the smaller is 0. The two endpoint samples also pull at gain 0.15 each. At W = 100, P = 1 and d = 0.5 m the centre pull is 360 internal force units, the same path wing forces take. magnet_force sets this pull, so it is not a holding force.

sections.title: Holding and release
sections.body: Once attached the pull stops and a Bullet hinge joint holds the parts. It keeps the two parts on one axis and lets them turn about it. The attach routine never reads magnet_force, and the joint's break threshold is the largest double, so the joint itself has no finite holding limit. Turning Magnet Toggle off or running out of electricity clears the connector's enable flag, and the next scene pass detaches it.

sections.title: Signals and transfers
sections.body: While linked, each update copies the composite signal, 32 on/off channels and 32 numbers, straight into the partner's Composite Data Receive and hands its video source to the partner's Video Data Receive. The copy has no buffer, scaling or averaging. The Electric port powers the magnet. This connector does not run the direct pool bridge that Electric Connectors and hardpoints use, so the port label alone does not show that electricity crosses the link.

limitations: Conversion of the pull, body weight and joint impulse to newtons and kilograms, signal and video timing across a link, the electrical link of small, hinge and large connectors, the Mag All's contact filtering and what ordnance does after Launch are listed as open items in the Magnetic connectors, transfers and hardpoints mechanics article.
Static analysis of one build. Forces and impulses are in the game's internal units; no attachment, pull or break was measured in a running game.

families.summary: Attaches to another Large Connector whose centre is under 0.25 m away and whose samples line up, then holds with a fixed joint. magnet_force 0.2 scales only the pull before attaching.

sections.title: Attaching
sections.body: It looks for another Large Connector within 10 m. It attaches when the two centres are under 0.25 m apart and each of its four rim samples, 0.25 m from the centre at quarter turns, lies within 0.1118 m of a rim sample on the other connector. With coincident centres that allows a twist of up to 25.8 degrees from any quarter turn (inference from the sample geometry). Both connectors need Magnet Toggle on, usable electricity, no existing link and different bodies.

sections.title: Pull before attaching
sections.body: Until it attaches, each update pulls toward the partner with F = 60 × 0.2 × P × W × d ÷ (1 + |d|²) for the offset d between matching samples, and nothing once |d| reaches 1 m. P is 1 with infinite electricity and otherwise max(0, (300 - EMP) ÷ 300) × charge fraction. W is the smaller of the two bodies' native weight field, or the larger when the smaller is 0. The four rim samples also pull at gain 0.15 each. At W = 100, P = 1 and d = 0.5 m the centre pull is 480 internal force units, the same path wing forces take. magnet_force sets this pull, so it is not a holding force.

sections.title: Holding and release
sections.body: Once attached the pull stops and a Bullet fixed joint holds the parts. It locks position and rotation. The attach routine never reads magnet_force, and the joint's break threshold is the largest double, so the joint itself has no finite holding limit. Turning Magnet Toggle off or running out of electricity clears the connector's enable flag, and the next scene pass detaches it.

sections.title: Signals and transfers
sections.body: While linked, each update copies the composite signal, 32 on/off channels and 32 numbers, straight into the partner's Composite Data Receive and hands its video source to the partner's Video Data Receive. The copy has no buffer, scaling or averaging. The Large Connector also sends On/Off Sent to the partner's On/Off Received and Number Sent to its Number Received, links its RPS shaft node to the partner's when both have one, and exchanges fluid between the two Fluid ports with factor 0.5 and bias 0, like the Fluid Connector. The networks stay separate. The Electric port powers the magnet. This connector does not run the direct pool bridge that Electric Connectors and hardpoints use, so the port label alone does not show that electricity crosses the link.

families.summary: Attaches to another Small Connector whose centre is under 0.5 m away, then holds with a point-to-point joint. magnet_force 0.1 scales only the pull before attaching.

sections.title: Attaching
sections.body: It looks for another Small Connector within 10 m and attaches when the two centres are under 0.5 m apart. There is no orientation test. Both connectors need Magnet Toggle on, usable electricity, no existing link and different bodies.

sections.title: Pull before attaching
sections.body: Until it attaches, each update pulls toward the partner with F = 60 × 0.1 × P × W × d ÷ (1 + |d|²) for the offset d between matching samples, and nothing once |d| reaches 1 m. P is 1 with infinite electricity and otherwise max(0, (300 - EMP) ÷ 300) × charge fraction. W is the smaller of the two bodies' native weight field, or the larger when the smaller is 0. At W = 100, P = 1 and d = 0.5 m the centre pull is 240 internal force units, the same path wing forces take. magnet_force sets this pull, so it is not a holding force. An EMP count of 150 with half charge gives P = 0.25 and cuts that to 60.

sections.title: Holding and release
sections.body: Once attached the pull stops and a Bullet point-to-point joint holds the parts. It pins the two centres together and leaves the parts free to turn. The attach routine never reads magnet_force, and the joint's break threshold is the largest double, so the joint itself has no finite holding limit. Turning Magnet Toggle off or running out of electricity clears the connector's enable flag, and the next scene pass detaches it.

sections.title: Signals and transfers
sections.body: While linked, each update copies the composite signal, 32 on/off channels and 32 numbers, straight into the partner's Composite Data Receive and hands its video source to the partner's Video Data Receive. The copy has no buffer, scaling or averaging. The Electric port powers the magnet. This connector does not run the direct pool bridge that Electric Connectors and hardpoints use, so the port label alone does not show that electricity crosses the link.

families.summary: Attaches to another Torque Connector whose centre is under 0.5 m away, with a point-to-point joint and no magnetic pull; Release detaches it and blocks reattaching for 120 updates.

sections.title: Attaching and release
sections.body: It looks for another Torque Connector within 10 m and attaches when the centres are under 0.5 m apart, with no orientation test. Its definition flag 0x100000 turns the magnetic pull off, so the parts must be brought that close. A Bullet point-to-point joint then pins the centres together and leaves the parts free to turn; its break threshold is the largest double, so the joint has no finite holding limit. Release starts a 120-update count, 2 simulated seconds. While it runs the connector cannot attach and the scene pass detaches it. Holding Release keeps restarting the count, so it can attach again 120 updates after the input goes off.

sections.title: Transfers
sections.body: While linked, the two connectors' shaft nodes are linked in the mechanical graph with a bridge parameter of 1000000 and a ratio field of 1. That parameter is not a power or torque rating. While linked, each update copies the composite signal, 32 on/off channels and 32 numbers, straight into the partner's Composite Data Receive and hands its video source to the partner's Video Data Receive. The copy has no buffer, scaling or averaging.

limitations: Conversion of the pull, body weight and joint impulse to newtons and kilograms, signal and video timing across a link, the electrical link of small, hinge and large connectors, the Mag All's contact filtering and what ordnance does after Launch are listed as open items in the Magnetic connectors, transfers and hardpoints mechanics article.
Static analysis of one build. Forces and impulses are in the game's internal units; no attachment, pull or break was measured in a running game.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: When attached, links its fluid network to the other connector's with bias 0, both directions and exchange factor 0.5; the two networks stay separate.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: With an attached connector, a network on its Fluid port and the transfer flag set, each update calls the two-port solver between the two Fluid ports: bias 0, both directions, all species and factor 0.5, which halves the per-update step limit. The connector holds no fluid and does not merge the networks, so each side keeps its own 40 L pipe pressure.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Free flow in the tooltip means no bias and no species filter. The halved step limit still applies, so it is not unlimited flow.

sections.title: Attaching and release
sections.body: It looks for another Fluid Connector within 10 m and attaches when the centres are under 0.5 m apart, with no orientation test. Its definition flag 0x100000 turns the magnetic pull off. A Bullet point-to-point joint then holds the centres together with no finite break threshold. Release starts a 120-update count, 2 simulated seconds. While it runs the connector cannot attach and the scene pass detaches it. Holding Release keeps restarting the count, so it can attach again 120 updates after the input goes off. While linked, each update copies the composite signal, 32 on/off channels and 32 numbers, straight into the partner's Composite Data Receive and hands its video source to the partner's Video Data Receive. The copy has no buffer, scaling or averaging.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Pumps heat from liquid A to liquid B by a fixed amount per update, even against the gradient, for 0.001 internal charge per update while switched on.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: With On/Off on, each update requests 0.001 internal charge, 0.06 per simulated second, through the shared draw helper, which takes min(0.001 × supply factor, pool charge). It pumps only when the returned share is above 0.1 and the two circuits together hold more than 0.001 liquid amount. Above that share the step is the full step; the request is made even when there is too little liquid to pump.

sections.title: Performance drivers
sections.body: Unlike an exchanger it does not stop at equal temperatures: A loses 0.03·qB/(qA+qB) and B gains 0.03·qA/(qA+qB) every update, so B can be driven hotter than A. While q stays constant, that is 1.8·qB/(qA+qB) and 1.8·qA/(qA+qB) per simulated second. Remove heat from B with a radiator or exchanger or the transfer stalls as B climbs.

sections.title: Capacity per litre
sections.body: q is the circuit's stored liquid amount: 0.1 per litre of fresh water, diesel, jet fuel, oil, seawater, slurry or saturated slurry, with no per-liquid factor. Gases add nothing. With 1 L in each circuit, qA = qB = 0.1, so each update moves A by -0.015 °C and B by +0.015 °C, -0.9 and +0.9 °C per simulated second, before both drift toward the surroundings by 0.001 of the gap.

families.summary: Moves at most 0.01 internal charge per update from its input network to its output network and never back. It checks no minimum charge difference.

sections.title: How the transfer works
sections.body: Each update the charger requests R = min(0.01, q_in, 1 − q_out), where q_in and q_out are the charge fractions of its two networks. It takes min(max(0, 1 − n ÷ 300) × q_in × R, E_in) from the input pool, n being its input node's EMP countdown and E_in the input pool's charge, and adds that to the output pool. Nothing moves once the output network is full or the input is empty. With infinite electricity it adds R without removing anything.

sections.title: Rates
sections.body: The cap is 0.01 per update, 0.6 per simulated second. Transfer runs even when the output is fuller than the input: at q_in = 0.5 and q_out = 0.9 it moves 0.005 per update, 0.3 per simulated second. Filling a small battery's 1600 from empty at the cap takes at least 2667 simulated seconds, so a charger suits trickle charging, not powering loads.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Use it to charge a battery from a generator bus without the battery back-feeding. Its electric node buffer is 0.01 (electric_type 6). The tooltip's significant discrepancy has no threshold in the code; the headroom and supply limits above take its place.

families.summary: Blinks for whole numbers of updates: on for trunc(60 × on time), off for trunc(60 × off time), while Control Signal is on.

sections.title: How it updates
sections.body: The two durations become N_on = trunc(60 × on time) and N_off = trunc(60 × off time) updates. When Control Signal changes the cycle counter restarts at 0. Otherwise the counter advances by 1 each update and wraps after N_on + N_off. The output is on while Control Signal is on and the counter is below N_on, so each cycle gives N_on updates on and N_off off. For example 0.51 s × 60 = 30.6, truncated to 30 updates.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The microprocessor Blinker is a different routine: it starts each call off and spends its wrap update off, so after the first cycle it gives one update fewer on.

families.summary: Turns on after Charge has been on for trunc(60 × charge time) updates and off after it has been off for trunc(60 × discharge time).

sections.title: How it updates
sections.body: Any change of Charge clears both counters. While the output is off and Charge is on, the charge counter is compared with N_charge, the output turns on when they are equal, then the counter adds 1. While the output is on and Charge is off, the discharge counter works the same way against N_discharge. With N_charge = 60 a rising Charge at update 0 turns the output on at update 60, the 61st update including the edge. A charge time of 0 turns it on in the edge update. For example 0.51 s × 60 = 30.6, truncated to 30 updates.

families.summary: Copies its input to the output once the input has stayed unchanged for trunc(60 × delay) updates; any change restarts the count.

sections.title: How it updates
sections.body: With N = trunc(60 × delay), a change of Signal to Delay resets the counter to 0 and leaves the output as it was. Each following update with the input unchanged adds 1, and when the counter reaches N the output takes the input. The output therefore follows a change N updates later, and a signal that flips sooner never passes. For example 0.51 s × 60 = 30.6, truncated to 30 updates. With N = 0 the output never changes, because the counter test c < N fails at once.

families.summary: Raises the input to the configured exponent; inputs below 1.1920929e-7 with an exponent below 1 output 0.

sections.title: How it updates
sections.body: When the input changes it outputs x^k through the C runtime powf. A guard outputs 0 instead when x is below 1.1920929e-7 and k below 1, which includes every negative input with such an exponent, or when |x| and k are both below 1.1920929e-7. So 0 to a negative power and 0 to the power 0 output 0, never infinity or 1. A negative base with a whole exponent of 1 or more keeps the usual sign: x = -2, k = 3 gives -8. A NaN result, such as a negative base with a fractional exponent of 1 or more, outputs 0, and so does an overflow to infinity.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Positive inputs from 1.1920929e-7 upward accept negative exponents: x = 4, k = -0.5 gives 0.5. For a signed square root or cube root, take |x| and restore the sign separately.

sections.title: Setup and interactions

families.summary: Per-update PID: Control Output = Ki·S + Kp·e + Kd·(e − e_prev), with e = Setpoint − Process Variable and S the running sum of e. There is no dt, no derivative filter and no output limit.

sections.title: How it updates
sections.body: Each update with Active on: e = Setpoint − Process Variable, S = S + e, d = e − e_prev, and Control Output = Ki × S + Kp × e + Kd × d. Arithmetic is single precision in that order. On the first update after Active turns on, d is 0. Turning Active off sets S, e_prev and the output to 0.

sections.title: Timebase
sections.body: Nothing is multiplied by a time step. S gains 60 errors per simulated second and d is the change over one update. Converting from per-second gains (an inference about tuning conventions, not engine code): Ki = Ki_per_second ÷ 60 and Kd = 60 × Kd_per_second. With Ki = 1 and a constant error of 1, the output reaches 60 after one simulated second.

sections.title: Limits and edge cases
sections.body: max_error (pid_controller_max_error) is the only limit. When it is above 0, S is clamped to ±max_error ÷ max(1e-8, Ki), so the integral term Ki × S stays within ±max_error for positive Ki. It does not limit P, D or Control Output. A NaN or infinite output becomes 0. The derivative acts on the error, so a Setpoint step gives a one-update kick of Kd × step.

sections.title: Microprocessor PIDs
sections.body: The microprocessor PID and advanced PID run the same recurrence without the max_error clamp and without the finite-value check, so their sum and output are unbounded. Example: Kp 2, Ki 0.5, Kd 0 and a steady error of 2 give 5, 6, 7 in a microprocessor; the physical PID with max_error 1 holds S at 2 and gives 5, 5, 5.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Set max_error to bound windup when the driven part saturates. Toggle Active off to clear the stored sum. Start with small Ki: a per-update sum grows 60 times faster than a per-second integral.

families.summary: Binds once to the nearest train junction within 30 units and flips that junction's route on each rising edge of Toggle Signal.

sections.title: How it updates
sections.body: On its first update the controller looks for the nearest junction with at least 3 connections strictly within 30 world units, keeps it, and writes its own route bit into it. It sets a searched flag even when it found nothing, so it never searches again. After that, each update where Toggle Signal changes to on flips the route bit and writes it into the junction. Turning the signal off, or holding it on, changes nothing. Trains read the junction's bit when they choose a branch there.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Place the controller within 30 units of the junction it should switch, and no nearer to another junction. Of two equally near junctions it keeps the first one stored. Each controller keeps its own route bit, so two controllers on one junction can disagree: each write replaces the junction's bit and the last write wins. Its tooltip and ports are word for word those of Push To Toggle.

families.summary: 800 m/s muzzle speed, 0.998 of its velocity kept per update, 0.02 heat per shot; lifetime 60 s.

sections.title: Ballistics
sections.body:
Muzzle speed 800 m/s plus the firing body's velocity. The round keeps 0.998 of its velocity each update and falls 0.5 m/s per update at sea level, and it is removed after 3600 updates (60 s); out of water it is not removed for being slow.

From 1 m above a flat sea-level plane: 0°: 211.3 m in 0.27 s, lands; 5°: 2690.8 m in 4.32 s, lands; 20°: 5161.3 m in 14.46 s, lands; 45°: 4519.6 m in 26.54 s, lands. Level from 100 m up, drop below the launch height: 100 m: 0.21 m at 0.126 s; 300 m: 2.07 m at 0.383 s; 500 m: 5.99 m at 0.649 s; 1000 m: 25.66 m at 1.353 s.

sections.title: Spread and recoil
sections.body: Two independent random angles of up to ±0.25 × 0.01 × m, so ±0.0025 rad per axis on a bare gun (0.002, 0.0015 and 0.00125 with 1, 2 and 3 or more extensions). A shot from a stationary gun pushes back with 80000 internal force units for one update.

sections.title: Loading and firing rate
sections.body: Breech transition 75 updates each way; after a round arrives the receiver waits 30 updates. Open Breech drives the breech, so the firing rate depends on how the loading is controlled.

sections.title: Heat
sections.body: Each shot adds 0.02 heat, which cools in 10 updates at 0.002 per update, much less than one breech transition, so it does not reach the stop at 1 (inference).

sections.title: Ammunition and fuses
sections.body: Impact magnitudes at muzzle speed: kinetic 0.8, AP 0.32, incendiary 0.52; HE 1 (broadphase 7.5 m), fragmentation 0.4 (3 m) plus 40 fragments. Fuse Timer applies to high-explosive and fragmentation rounds.

findings.detail: The worker converts its tick count (worker+0xd0, loaded at 0x1405e3ad7) to binary32 and divides it by this, then passes the widened result as the elapsed time to the physics world's stepSimulation slot +0x60 at 0x1405e3b16, with at most 1000 solver substeps. limitations: Belt throughput, controlled cannon cadence and final target damage are open items listed under Weapons on the parts index.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: 900 m/s muzzle speed, 0.995 of its velocity kept per update, 0.08 heat per shot; removed below 50 m/s or after 10 s.

sections.title: Ballistics
sections.body:
Muzzle speed 900 m/s plus the firing body's velocity. The round keeps 0.995 of its velocity each update and falls 0.5 m/s per update at sea level, and it is removed after 600 updates (10 s) or once it slows below 50 m/s.

From 1 m above a flat sea-level plane: 0°: 234.2 m in 0.27 s, lands; 5°: 2186.1 m in 4.37 s, lands; 20°: 2679.8 m in 10.00 s, lifetime ends at 301 m height; 45°: 2016.5 m in 10.00 s, lifetime ends at 1348 m height. Level from 100 m up, drop below the launch height: 100 m: 0.16 m at 0.113 s; 300 m: 1.69 m at 0.350 s; 500 m: 5.03 m at 0.606 s; 1000 m: 23.56 m at 1.348 s.

sections.title: Spread and recoil
sections.body: Two independent random angles of up to ±0.25 × 0.01 × m, so ±0.0025 rad per axis on a bare gun (0.002, 0.0015 and 0.00125 with 1, 2 and 3 or more extensions). A shot from a stationary gun pushes back with 22500 internal force units for one update.

sections.title: Loading and firing rate
sections.body: Breech transition 16 updates, receiver delay 6. Inference, not a measurement: with a round always ready it cycles every 38 updates, 94.737 rounds per minute.

sections.title: Heat
sections.body: Each shot adds 0.08 heat and every update removes 0.002. At 1 it stops firing until heat is below 0.25. With ideal feeding and the trigger held it does not reach 1 within 120 s (inference).

sections.title: Ammunition and fuses
sections.body: Impact magnitudes at muzzle speed: kinetic 0.54, AP 0.216, incendiary 0.351; HE 0.6 (broadphase 4.5 m), fragmentation 0.24 (1.8 m) plus 12 fragments. Fuse Timer applies to high-explosive and fragmentation rounds.

limitations: Belt throughput, controlled cannon cadence and final target damage are open items listed under Weapons on the parts index.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

sections.title: Ballistics
sections.body:
Muzzle speed 1000 m/s plus the firing body's velocity. The round keeps 0.98 of its velocity each update and falls 0.5 m/s per update at sea level, and it is removed after 300 updates (5 s) or once it slows below 50 m/s.

From 1 m above a flat sea-level plane: 0°: 241.5 m in 0.28 s, lands; 5°: 792.4 m in 2.55 s, removed below 50 m/s at 27 m height; 20°: 742.1 m in 2.43 s, removed below 50 m/s at 231 m height; 45°: 552.2 m in 2.28 s, removed below 50 m/s at 517 m height. Level from 100 m up, drop below the launch height: 100 m: 0.13 m at 0.105 s; 300 m: 1.67 m at 0.368 s; 500 m: 6.26 m at 0.756 s; 1000 m: removed before it gets there.

sections.title: Spread and recoil
sections.body: Two independent random angles of up to ±0.25 × 0.01 × m, so ±0.0025 rad per axis on a bare gun (0.002, 0.0015 and 0.00125 with 1, 2 and 3 or more extensions). A shot from a stationary gun pushes back with 10000 internal force units for one update.

sections.title: Loading and firing rate
sections.body: Breech transition 4 updates, receiver delay 0. Inference, not a measurement: with a round always ready it cycles every 8 updates, 450 rounds per minute.

sections.title: Heat
sections.body: Each shot adds 0.025 heat and every update removes 0.002. At 1 it stops firing until heat is below 0.25. With ideal feeding and the trigger held it stops on shot 110, 872 updates (14.53 s) after the first shot; fires again 377 updates (6.283 s) later (inference).

sections.title: Ammunition and fuses
sections.body: Impact magnitudes at muzzle speed: kinetic 0.2, AP 0.08, incendiary 0.13; HE 0.2 (broadphase 1.5 m), fragmentation 0.08 (0.6 m) plus 2 fragments. Fuse Timer applies to fragmentation rounds only; high-explosive rounds on this gun ignore it.

limitations: Belt throughput, controlled cannon cadence and final target damage are open items listed under Weapons on the parts index.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: 1000 m/s rounds every 2 updates at best (inference); heat rises 0.01 per shot and falls 0.002 per update, so it stops on shot 166 and fires again once heat is below 0.25.

sections.title: Ballistics
sections.body:
Muzzle speed 1000 m/s plus the firing body's velocity. The round keeps 0.99 of its velocity each update and falls 0.5 m/s per update at sea level, and it is removed after 300 updates (5 s) or once it slows below 50 m/s.

From 1 m above a flat sea-level plane: 0°: 253.9 m in 0.27 s, lands; 5°: 1534.1 m in 4.27 s, lands; 20°: 1489.3 m in 5.00 s, lifetime ends at 375 m height; 45°: 1095.5 m in 4.40 s, removed below 50 m/s at 957 m height. Level from 100 m up, drop below the launch height: 100 m: 0.13 m at 0.103 s; 300 m: 1.44 m at 0.329 s; 500 m: 4.52 m at 0.592 s; 1000 m: 25.68 m at 1.520 s.

sections.title: Spread and recoil
sections.body: Two independent random angles of up to ±0.25 × 0.02 × m, so ±0.005 rad per axis on a bare gun (0.004, 0.003 and 0.0025 with 1, 2 and 3 or more extensions). A shot from a stationary gun pushes back with 15000 internal force units for one update.

sections.title: Loading and firing rate
sections.body: Breech transition 1 update, receiver delay 0. Inference, not a measurement: with a round always ready it cycles every 2 updates, 1800 rounds per minute. The barrels spin up for 30 updates before the first shot.

sections.title: Overheat cycle
sections.body: With ideal feeding and the trigger held it stops on shot 166, 330 updates (5.5 s) after the first shot; fires again 376 updates (6.267 s) later. Startup, belt routing and slower feeding change these times and can keep it below the stop. Releasing the trigger earlier lets heat fall 0.12 per second; firing short bursts keeps it running.

sections.title: Ammunition and fuses
sections.body: Impact magnitudes at muzzle speed: kinetic 0.3, AP 0.12, incendiary 0.195; HE 0.3 (broadphase 2.25 m), fragmentation 0.12 (0.9 m) plus 2 fragments. Fuse Timer applies to fragmentation rounds only; high-explosive rounds on this gun ignore it.

limitations: Belt throughput, controlled cannon cadence and final target damage are open items listed under Weapons on the parts index.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: 700 m/s muzzle speed, 0.999 of its velocity kept per update, 0.02 heat per shot; lifetime 60 s.

sections.title: Ballistics
sections.body:
Muzzle speed 700 m/s plus the firing body's velocity. The round keeps 0.999 of its velocity each update and falls 0.5 m/s per update at sea level, and it is removed after 3600 updates (60 s); out of water it is not removed for being slow.

From 1 m above a flat sea-level plane: 0°: 185.8 m in 0.27 s, lands; 5°: 2455.2 m in 3.95 s, lands; 20°: 6272.4 m in 14.14 s, lands; 45°: 6614.0 m in 26.96 s, lands. Level from 100 m up, drop below the launch height: 100 m: 0.27 m at 0.143 s; 300 m: 2.69 m at 0.434 s; 500 m: 7.68 m at 0.730 s; 1000 m: 32.03 m at 1.493 s.

sections.title: Spread and recoil
sections.body: Two independent random angles of up to ±0.25 × 0.005 × m, so ±0.00125 rad per axis on a bare gun (0.001, 0.00075 and 0.000625 with 1, 2 and 3 or more extensions). A shot from a stationary gun pushes back with 140000 internal force units for one update.

sections.title: Loading and firing rate
sections.body: Breech transition 250 updates each way; after a round arrives the receiver waits 90 updates. Open Breech drives the breech, so the firing rate depends on how the loading is controlled.

sections.title: Heat
sections.body: Each shot adds 0.02 heat, which cools in 10 updates at 0.002 per update, much less than one breech transition, so it does not reach the stop at 1 (inference).

sections.title: Ammunition and fuses
sections.body: Impact magnitudes at muzzle speed: kinetic 1.4, AP 0.56, incendiary 0.91; HE 2 (broadphase 15 m), fragmentation 0.8 (6 m) plus 60 fragments. Fuse Timer applies to high-explosive and fragmentation rounds.

limitations: Belt throughput, controlled cannon cadence and final target damage are open items listed under Weapons on the parts index.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: 800 m/s muzzle speed, 0.975 of its velocity kept per update, 0.0125 heat per shot; removed below 50 m/s or after 5 s.

sections.title: Ballistics
sections.body:
Muzzle speed 800 m/s plus the firing body's velocity. The round keeps 0.975 of its velocity each update and falls 0.5 m/s per update at sea level, and it is removed after 300 updates (5 s) or once it slows below 50 m/s.

From 1 m above a flat sea-level plane: 0°: 188.2 m in 0.29 s, lands; 5°: 500.1 m in 1.87 s, removed below 50 m/s at 21 m height; 20°: 468.6 m in 1.80 s, removed below 50 m/s at 149 m height; 45°: 348.6 m in 1.70 s, removed below 50 m/s at 329 m height. Level from 100 m up, drop below the launch height: 100 m: 0.23 m at 0.137 s; 300 m: 3.30 m at 0.544 s; 500 m: 23.37 m at 1.825 s; 1000 m: removed before it gets there.

sections.title: Spread and recoil
sections.body: Two independent random angles of up to ±0.25 × 0.01 × m, so ±0.0025 rad per axis on a bare gun (0.002, 0.0015 and 0.00125 with 1, 2 and 3 or more extensions). A shot from a stationary gun pushes back with 4000 internal force units for one update.

sections.title: Loading and firing rate
sections.body: Breech transition 2 updates, receiver delay 0. Inference, not a measurement: with a round always ready it cycles every 4 updates, 900 rounds per minute.

sections.title: Heat
sections.body: Each shot adds 0.0125 heat and every update removes 0.002. At 1 it stops firing until heat is below 0.25. With ideal feeding and the trigger held it stops on shot 221, 880 updates (14.67 s) after the first shot; fires again 377 updates (6.283 s) later (inference).

sections.title: Ammunition and fuses
sections.body: Impact magnitudes at muzzle speed: kinetic 0.08, AP 0.032, incendiary 0.052; no HE or fragmentation blast (explosive support 0). It has no explosive rounds, so Fuse Timer has no effect.

limitations: Belt throughput, controlled cannon cadence and final target damage are open items listed under Weapons on the parts index.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: 600 m/s muzzle speed, 0.9995 of its velocity kept per update, 0.02 heat per shot; lifetime 60 s.

sections.title: Ballistics
sections.body:
Muzzle speed 600 m/s plus the firing body's velocity. The round keeps 0.9995 of its velocity each update and falls 0.5 m/s per update at sea level, and it is removed after 3600 updates (60 s); out of water it is not removed for being slow.

From 1 m above a flat sea-level plane: 0°: 159.6 m in 0.27 s, lands; 5°: 1968.3 m in 3.47 s, lands; 20°: 6054.2 m in 12.96 s, lands; 45°: 7606.4 m in 25.72 s, lands. Level from 100 m up, drop below the launch height: 100 m: 0.38 m at 0.167 s; 300 m: 3.66 m at 0.504 s; 500 m: 10.36 m at 0.844 s; 1000 m: 42.61 m at 1.709 s.

sections.title: Spread and recoil
sections.body: Two independent random angles of up to ±0.25 × 0.005 × m, so ±0.00125 rad per axis on a bare gun (0.001, 0.00075 and 0.000625 with 1, 2 and 3 or more extensions). A shot from a stationary gun pushes back with 240000 internal force units for one update.

sections.title: Loading and firing rate
sections.body: Breech transition 600 updates each way; after a round arrives the receiver waits 240 updates. Open Breech drives the breech, so the firing rate depends on how the loading is controlled.

sections.title: Heat
sections.body: Each shot adds 0.02 heat, which cools in 10 updates at 0.002 per update, much less than one breech transition, so it does not reach the stop at 1 (inference).

sections.title: Ammunition and fuses
sections.body: Impact magnitudes at muzzle speed: kinetic 2.4, AP 0.96, incendiary 1.56; HE 4 (broadphase 30 m), fragmentation 1.6 (12 m) plus 80 fragments. Fuse Timer applies to high-explosive and fragmentation rounds.

families.summary: Each update one fixed reaction turns 0.000165 amount of oxygen and 0.00033 of hydrogen into 0.03 of water and 1 internal charge: at most 5.94 L/s of oxygen and 11.88 L/s of hydrogen into 18 L/s of water and 60 charge/s.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Pair with an electrolyser, which splits fresh water into hydrogen and oxygen using electricity.

sections.title: Reaction
sections.body: One inlet takes only oxygen and the other only hydrogen into a shared buffer. An undamaged cell then runs at most one reaction per update: it needs at least 0.000165 amount of oxygen (0.099 expanded litres), 0.00033 of hydrogen (0.198 L) and 0.03 of free space in its water buffer (0.3 L). It removes both gases, adds 0.03 amount of fresh water and deposits 1 internal charge into the electrical network. Water leaves through the outlet port; if it backs up until less than 0.03 is free, reactions stop.

sections.title: Rates
sections.body: At 60 reactions per simulated second the cell uses 5.94 L/s of oxygen and 11.88 L/s of hydrogen, measured as expanded gas, and makes 18 L/s of water and 60 charge/s. Over 600 reactions, 10 simulated seconds, that is 59.4 L and 118.8 L of gas, 180 L of water and 600 charge. These are ceilings: thin gas supply or a full water buffer skips reactions.

sections.title: Electrical output
sections.body: The cell does not check battery demand. It deposits the charge whenever it reacts, and with no electrical network attached the charge is dropped while the gases are still used.

sections.title: Space DLC
sections.body: The reaction runs only when the Space DLC is owned and enabled in the current session, the same gate the electrolyser and the directional antennas use. Without it the cell makes no water or charge.

limitations: Static analysis of one build. Charge is in the game's internal electrical units, as on the Electricity pages; fluid amounts are stored amounts, 10 L of liquid or 600 L of expanded gas per amount.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Ignites above 0.5 RPS, then burns 0.12 × throttle × RPS L/s of jet fuel and adds 1600 × throttle × RPS pressure and 0.1 × throttle × RPS temperature per update.

sections.title: Ignition
sections.body: Combustion runs only while the chamber's RPS is strictly above 0.5. There is no pressure, temperature or spark test, so the tooltip's internal pressure threshold is in effect the compressor's job of spinning the shared RPS past 0.5.

sections.title: Fuel use
sections.body: Fuel per update is 0.0002 × RPS amount × u, with u = clamp(Throttle, 0, 1) further limited by the jet fuel in the 4 L buffer: 0.12 × u × RPS L/s, 2.4 L/s at 20 RPS and full throttle. With only 0.01 L left at 20 RPS, u drops to 0.25 and the update burns it. infinite_fuel skips the limit and the debit. Other liquids in the buffer are cleared.

sections.title: Pressure and heat
sections.body: Above 0.5 RPS: outgoing pressure = incoming + 1600 × u × RPS and outgoing temperature = incoming + 0.1 × u × RPS, in internal units; the incoming pressure is then cleared. At 20 RPS and full throttle from zero that is 32000 and 2 in one update.

sections.title: Overspeed
sections.body:
With the engine_overheating and vehicle_damage settings both on, a chamber above 200 internal RPS sets a one-time latch and requests its own damage + 1. A routine passes that request through the connected jet parts in both directions, and each part keeps the larger of its own damage and the request, capped at 50. An undamaged chamber therefore raises itself and every jet part joined to it to at least 1 damage on its first overspeed.

In the jet update, any damage stops a turbine from turning pressure into RPS, so 1 is enough. Existing speed and the pressure already in the engine are not cleared, and the chamber keeps burning fuel and adding pressure, so the engine is not shut down at once; it loses the turbines' pressure-driven speed gain. The branch also queues visual effects, but it makes no area damage and does not reset engine speed.

Repairing a turbine to 0 damage restores its gain. Repairing the chamber to 0 clears the latch, so the next overspeed damages again; it does not repair the other parts.

limitations: Static decompilation of one build; the game was not run. Figures are for one part in one update. What an assembled engine settles at depends on its duct network; the Jet engines category lists that and the unit questions as open.
Pressure, temperature, charge and force are internal units, not pascals, degrees, watts or newtons.
The overspeed branch's visual and sound effects and the repair tool's rate are outside this decode.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Spins up from electricity and pushes pressure forward: q = 0.2 × (100 × RPS - pressure rise) per update, losing 0.0001 × q RPS for it.

sections.title: Starting
sections.body: With the Compressor input on and electricity connected the compressor requests 0.1 charge every update (6 per simulated second) and adds 0.01 × the supplied fraction to its RPS. Its electric_magnitude of 0 is not used. Speed is then multiplied by 0.99, enabled or not.

sections.title: Pressure and load
sections.body: After averaging with its neighbours the compressor aims for a pressure rise of 100 × RPS across itself and moves 0.2 of the shortfall from its incoming to its outgoing side. Back pressure above that target makes q negative, so pressure flows backwards and the compressor speeds up. q is a pressure transfer, not a volume flow in L/s.

sections.title: Example
sections.body: From rest with full supply the first update gives r0 = 0.0099 RPS, q = 0.198 and r_local = 0.0098802. The averaging with neighbours then changes the next state, so this is not a startup time.

limitations: Static decompilation of one build; the game was not run. Figures are for one part in one update. What an assembled engine settles at depends on its duct network; the Jet engines category lists that and the unit questions as open.
Pressure, temperature, charge and force are internal units, not pascals, degrees, watts or newtons.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: The basic exhaust's force times 1 + 500 × the jet fuel stored in its buffer while Afterburner is on; its branch never subtracts that fuel.

sections.title: Thrust
sections.body: Force = 32 × (incoming pressure - 1000) × a × b × (1 - Thrust Spoiler) along the exhaust's thrust axis, with altitude factor a = clamp(1 - height × 1.5 ÷ 40000, 0, 1) and afterburner multiplier b = 1 when off. At or below 1000 there is no force. No exhaust size, engine_max_force or RPS term enters; RPS matters only through the pressure the chamber adds upstream.

sections.title: Afterburner multiplier
sections.body: With the Afterburner input on and any liquid in its buffer, b = 1 + 0.5 × stored jet fuel ÷ 0.001 = 1 + 500 × stored amount. 0.001 amount (0.01 L) gives 1.5; a full 0.4 amount (4 L) buffer gives 201. The ratio has no upper clamp, so a full buffer multiplies thrust far beyond the tooltip's description, until the 100 × S cap.

sections.title: Fuel
sections.body:
Jet fuel reaches the 4 L buffer through the Fuel port. Each update the port exchange moves liquid between the pipe network and the buffer with a pressure bias of -10, in either direction, so it can fill the buffer or send fuel back. A purge then removes up to 0.001 of every other liquid and skips jet fuel. The multiplier reads the stored jet fuel and subtracts none.

So the afterburner burns no fuel of its own: 0 L/s at a steady buffer level. Fuel flows through the port only while the buffer fills, drains back or the network changes. The tooltip's increased fuel consumption has no counterpart in this update; more stored fuel gives more thrust, not more burn.

Outside the update, the constructor empties the buffer and the jet serializer saves the Fuel port state but not the buffer. A whole-executable search for stores to the buffer's jet fuel found no other debit of the afterburner's fuel.

sections.title: Force units and limit
sections.body: The force is in internal units. Before it is applied its size is limited to 100 × S, the same mechanism the control surfaces use with a limit of 5. S is the summed adjusted mass of every body joined to this one by joints, free or locked, so all of them share one S; the Control surfaces category gives the rule and examples. With one body of mass 1000, S = 1000 and the cap is 100000. It is applied once per update and integrated by the physics solver; do not multiply it by 60.

sections.title: Example
sections.body: At incoming pressure 16000, sea level and spoiler 0 the force is 480000; spoiler 0.5 gives 240000. With S = 1000 the cap limits both to 100000. An enabled afterburner holding 0.01 L gives 720000 before the cap.

findings.detail: The substep is 1 ÷ the worker's solver rate (worker+0xb8), or binary32 1/60 from 0x140baf98c in the fallback branch at 0x1405e3af4. limitations: Static decompilation of one build; the game was not run. Figures are for one part in one update. What an assembled engine settles at depends on its duct network; the Jet engines category lists that and the unit questions as open.
Pressure, temperature, charge and force are internal units, not pascals, degrees, watts or newtons.

Writes to the exhaust's fuel buffer through escaped pointers, generic copies or computed addresses were not traced, so an indirect writer elsewhere is not ruled out. Transient Fuel port flow while the buffer fills or returns fuel depends on the connected network.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Pushes with 32 × (incoming pressure - 1000), scaled by altitude and the Thrust Spoiler, capped at 100 × S.

sections.title: Thrust
sections.body: Force = 32 × (incoming pressure - 1000) × a × b × (1 - Thrust Spoiler) along the exhaust's thrust axis, with altitude factor a = clamp(1 - height × 1.5 ÷ 40000, 0, 1) and afterburner multiplier b = 1 when off. At or below 1000 there is no force. No exhaust size, engine_max_force or RPS term enters; RPS matters only through the pressure the chamber adds upstream.

sections.title: Altitude and spoiler
sections.body: The altitude factor falls linearly to 0 at a height of 26666.67 and is 0.625 at 10000. Reading that height as metres is an inference. Thrust Spoiler 0 keeps the whole force and 1 removes it, without changing engine speed. Above 1000 the exhaust clears its incoming pressure each update after using it.

sections.title: Force units and limit
sections.body: The force is in internal units. Before it is applied its size is limited to 100 × S, the same mechanism the control surfaces use with a limit of 5. S is the summed adjusted mass of every body joined to this one by joints, free or locked, so all of them share one S; the Control surfaces category gives the rule and examples. With one body of mass 1000, S = 1000 and the cap is 100000. It is applied once per update and integrated by the physics solver; do not multiply it by 60.

sections.title: Example
sections.body: At incoming pressure 16000, sea level and spoiler 0 the force is 480000; spoiler 0.5 gives 240000. With S = 1000 the cap limits both to 100000.

findings.detail: Builds one integer label per vehicle body (assembly +0x18). limitations: Static decompilation of one build; the game was not run. Figures are for one part in one update. What an assembled engine settles at depends on its duct network; the Jet engines category lists that and the unit questions as open.
Pressure, temperature, charge and force are internal units, not pascals, degrees, watts or newtons.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: The basic exhaust's force along a direction set by a powered pivot within −0.5 … 0.5 turns.

sections.title: Thrust
sections.body: Force = 32 × (incoming pressure - 1000) × a × b × (1 - Thrust Spoiler) along the exhaust's thrust axis, with altitude factor a = clamp(1 - height × 1.5 ÷ 40000, 0, 1) and afterburner multiplier b = 1 when off. At or below 1000 there is no force. No exhaust size, engine_max_force or RPS term enters; RPS matters only through the pressure the chamber adds upstream. The pivot turns the thrust axis and the lever arm; the coefficient is the same as the basic exhaust's.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Rotation Target is a standard value; supply Electric for the pivot.

sections.title: Force units and limit
sections.body: The force is in internal units. Before it is applied its size is limited to 100 × S, the same mechanism the control surfaces use with a limit of 5. S is the summed adjusted mass of every body joined to this one by joints, free or locked, so all of them share one S; the Control surfaces category gives the rule and examples. With one body of mass 1000, S = 1000 and the cap is 100000. It is applied once per update and integrated by the physics solver; do not multiply it by 60.

families.summary: Reports the laser point closest to its view centre inside a 120 degree cone, as x and y direction components divided by cos(0.5 rad); the outputs are not angles.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Composite number channels 1 and 2 give x and y; on/off channel 1 is set while a point is visible. Match the Wavelength input to the emitting beacon or laser.

sections.title: Field of view and outputs
sections.body: The sensor accepts a point when the dot product of the unit direction to it with the sensor's forward axis is above 0.5, which means less than 60 degrees from forward: the 120 degree field of view the Data Output port states. Of the accepted points it reports the one with the largest dot product. Channel 1 is the direction's x component and channel 2 its y component, each divided by 0.87758255, the tooltip's cos(0.5). Both statements hold: 120 degrees is the cone, and cos(0.5) is only the output scale. A point 30 degrees to one side reads 0.569747; at the edge of the cone the output reaches 0.986831, never 1. For a point on one axis, the angle from forward is asin(0.87758255 × output) (inference from the projection).

families.summary: Up/Down track: each input drives the head one way at W × A × 5 ÷ r m/s, with force cap 20000 × r × P.

sections.title: How it moves
sections.body: Up and Down push in opposite directions; both or neither give zero speed, and the motor then holds the head with its force cap. Speed W × A × 5 ÷ r m/s. At W = A = 1 that is 5 at 1:1, 2.5 at 1:2, 1.25 at 1:4, 0.625 at 1:8, 0.3125 at 1:16, 0.15625 at 1:32 m/s. Travel comes from the track: each aligned base or extension block adds 0.25 m in its direction.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The force cap is 20000 × r × P without availability. With Max Power 100% it is 20000 at 1:1, 40000 at 1:2, 80000 at 1:4, 160000 at 1:8, 320000 at 1:16, 640000 at 1:32. Each update requests 0.01 × |c × 5| electricity while moving.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The RPS port passes mechanical power across the joint. The Fluid port carries fluid across the joint through the shared two-port solver, both ways, all species, with no bias and flow factor 1, so the joint itself adds no restriction. Delivered flow still follows the pressures on both sides. The motor does not read that pressure.

findings.label: Linear Track Base rule

findings.label: Linear Track Base · tooltip
findings.value: You can build the track using the Linear Track Extension component. This base component provides 3 blocks that can be built on. A pair of on/off signals allow you to control the up and down motion of the slider, and a numerical output lets you measure the slider's offset from its starting position. Multiple slider bases can run along the same track. The up/down speed can be configured by selecting this component with the select tool.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. families.summary: Speed-controlled track: Slider Speed s moves the head at s × 5 ÷ r m/s with force cap A × 10000 × r × P.

sections.title: How it moves
sections.body: Slider Speed is clamped to −1 … 1, then the head moves at clamp(s × 5 ÷ r, −10, 10) m/s. At s = 1 that is 5 at 1:1, 2.5 at 1:2, 1.25 at 1:4, 0.625 at 1:8, 0.3125 at 1:16, 0.15625 at 1:32 m/s. Travel comes from the track: each aligned base or extension block adds 0.25 m in its direction.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The force cap is A × 10000 × r × P. At A = P = 1 it is 10000 at 1:1, 20000 at 1:2, 40000 at 1:4, 80000 at 1:8, 160000 at 1:16, 320000 at 1:32. At s = 0 it holds with this cap. Each update requests 0.01 × |v| electricity.

findings.label: Compact Linear Track Base rule

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Moving head of the Compact Linear Track Base. Speed-controlled track: Slider Speed s moves the head at s × 5 ÷ r m/s with force cap A × 10000 × r × P.

sections.title: What drives it
sections.body: This is the moving half that Compact Linear Track Base places as its child_name. The base runs the motor; this definition carries flag 0x80 without the powered bit, so its own motor fields do not set the joint's performance.

sections.title: Assembled joint
sections.body: Speed-controlled track: Slider Speed s moves the head at s × 5 ÷ r m/s with force cap A × 10000 × r × P. Slider Speed is clamped to −1 … 1, then the head moves at clamp(s × 5 ÷ r, −10, 10) m/s. At s = 1 that is 5 at 1:1, 2.5 at 1:2, 1.25 at 1:4, 0.625 at 1:8, 0.3125 at 1:16, 0.15625 at 1:32 m/s. Travel comes from the track: each aligned base or extension block adds 0.25 m in its direction.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The force cap is A × 10000 × r × P. At A = P = 1 it is 10000 at 1:1, 20000 at 1:2, 40000 at 1:4, 80000 at 1:8, 160000 at 1:16, 320000 at 1:32. At s = 0 it holds with this cap. Each update requests 0.01 × |v| electricity.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. families.summary: Moving head of the Linear Track Base. Up/Down track: each input drives the head one way at W × A × 5 ÷ r m/s, with force cap 20000 × r × P.

sections.title: What drives it
sections.body: This is the moving half that Linear Track Base places as its child_name. The base runs the motor; this definition carries flag 0x80 without the powered bit, so its own motor fields do not set the joint's performance.

sections.title: Assembled joint
sections.body: Up/Down track: each input drives the head one way at W × A × 5 ÷ r m/s, with force cap 20000 × r × P. Up and Down push in opposite directions; both or neither give zero speed, and the motor then holds the head with its force cap. Speed W × A × 5 ÷ r m/s. At W = A = 1 that is 5 at 1:1, 2.5 at 1:2, 1.25 at 1:4, 0.625 at 1:8, 0.3125 at 1:16, 0.15625 at 1:32 m/s. Travel comes from the track: each aligned base or extension block adds 0.25 m in its direction.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The force cap is 20000 × r × P without availability. With Max Power 100% it is 20000 at 1:1, 40000 at 1:2, 80000 at 1:4, 160000 at 1:8, 320000 at 1:16, 640000 at 1:32. Each update requests 0.01 × |c × 5| electricity while moving.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The RPS port passes mechanical power across the joint. The Fluid port carries fluid across the joint through the shared two-port solver, both ways, all species, with no bias and flow factor 1, so the joint itself adds no restriction. Delivered flow still follows the pressures on both sides. The motor does not read that pressure.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Electric position servo over ±0.5 m: force cap 200000 × r × P, speed up to W × 5 ÷ r m/s.

sections.title: How it moves
sections.body: The target position is 0.5 × 1 × s = 0.5 × s m, with hard stops at ±0.5 m. Each update it aims for c × 5 ÷ r m/s with c = clamp(10 × (s − x ÷ 0.5), −W, W), where x is the rod position and W the Speed setting (0.1 to 5, default 1). The motor reads electricity, not fluid pressure, despite the name.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The force cap is 200000 × r × P. With Max Power 100% it is 200000 at 1:1, 400000 at 1:2, 800000 at 1:4, 1600000 at 1:8, 3200000 at 1:16, 6400000 at 1:32. Availability does not lower it. Each update requests 0.01 × |c × 5| electricity.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The Fluid port carries fluid across the joint through the shared two-port solver, both ways, all species, with no bias and flow factor 1, so the joint itself adds no restriction. Delivered flow still follows the pressures on both sides. The motor does not read that pressure. Piston Rod Position reports σ × x in metres.

The piston's speed can be configured by selecting it with the select tool.

findings.label: Ticks per simulated second
findings.detail: The worker converts its tick count (worker+0xd0, loaded at 0x1405e3ad7) to binary32 and divides it by this, then passes the widened result as the elapsed time to the physics world's stepSimulation slot +0x60 at 0x1405e3b16, with at most 1000 solver substeps. With tick count 1 the elapsed simulated time is 1/60 s. Report: investigation/update-rate.md. findings.label: Solver substep
findings.detail: The substep is 1 ÷ the worker's solver rate (worker+0xb8), or binary32 1/60 from 0x140baf98c in the fallback branch at 0x1405e3af4. The accumulator 0x140133ea0 runs whole substeps of that length. The component dispatch is outside that loop, so the solver rates 60, 120 and 180 chosen by the coordinator do not multiply component updates. Report: investigation/update-rate.md. limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Moving head of the Pneumatic Piston. Electric position servo over ±0.5 m: force cap 200000 × r × P, speed up to W × 5 ÷ r m/s.

sections.title: What drives it
sections.body: This is the moving half that Pneumatic Piston places as its child_name. The base runs the motor; this definition carries flag 0x80 without the powered bit, so its own motor fields do not set the joint's performance.

sections.title: Assembled joint
sections.body: Electric position servo over ±0.5 m: force cap 200000 × r × P, speed up to W × 5 ÷ r m/s. The target position is 0.5 × 1 × s = 0.5 × s m, with hard stops at ±0.5 m. Each update it aims for c × 5 ÷ r m/s with c = clamp(10 × (s − x ÷ 0.5), −W, W), where x is the rod position and W the Speed setting (0.1 to 5, default 1). The motor reads electricity, not fluid pressure, despite the name.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The force cap is 200000 × r × P. With Max Power 100% it is 200000 at 1:1, 400000 at 1:2, 800000 at 1:4, 1600000 at 1:8, 3200000 at 1:16, 6400000 at 1:32. Availability does not lower it. Each update requests 0.01 × |c × 5| electricity.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The Fluid port carries fluid across the joint through the shared two-port solver, both ways, all species, with no bias and flow factor 1, so the joint itself adds no restriction. Delivered flow still follows the pressures on both sides. The motor does not read that pressure.

families.summary: Outputs the physics velocity of the point where it sits, in m/s, in one of four modes: full speed, along its own axis, horizontal or vertical.

sections.title: Reading
sections.body:
Logic case 19 takes the body's linear velocity plus its angular velocity × the lever arm from the body origin to the sensor: the velocity of that point in the current physics state. It does not difference positions over time and does not subtract wind, so it reads speed over the ground, not airspeed.

Mode 0 outputs the length of that velocity, mode 1 its signed component along the sensor's own axis, mode 2 the horizontal speed sqrt(vx² + vz²) and mode 3 the vertical component vy. Any other mode value gives 0. Above a world height of 40000 the output is 0.

sections.title: Placement
sections.body: Because the angular term is included, a sensor far from the centre of a turning or rolling vehicle reads more than one near the centre.

sections.title: Timing
sections.body: There is no sensor timer, history or smoothing. The value is recomputed on every logic update, 60 per simulated second, and written only when it changes.

families.summary: Grabs what touches a 0.125 m contact sphere at its face, holds it with a point-to-point joint and lets go when Force, the joint's solver impulse, exceeds 200 × electrical supply.

sections.title: Grabbing
sections.body: While Magnet Toggle is on, the Mag All keeps a Bullet contact sphere of radius 0.125 m at its magnet face. A body it touches, static or moving, is joined to it with a point-to-point joint. There is no pull from a distance, and its magnet_force field of 0.1 is never read by its update.

sections.title: Force and breaking
sections.body: Force reports the absolute applied impulse that the physics solver last computed for that joint, in internal units. It is an impulse per solver step and is not divided by the time step, so it is not a force in newtons. With no link Force is 0. The joint lets go when Force exceeds 200 × P, where P is 1 with infinite electricity and otherwise max(0, (300 - EMP) ÷ 300) × charge fraction. At full supply 200 holds and 201 breaks, as the tooltip's 200 suggests. At P = 0.25, from an EMP count of 150 and half charge, the threshold is 50. After a break it waits 30 updates, 0.5 simulated seconds, before it can grab again.

Static analysis of one build. Forces and impulses are in the game's internal units; no attachment, pull or break was measured in a running game.

For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.
