families.summary: A microcontroller in a block: each update it copies its connected inputs into an embedded logic graph, runs the graph, then copies the graph outputs back out. Composite bridges copy all 32 on/off and 32 number channels, video bridges a descriptor and audio bridges the samples.

sections.title: How it updates
sections.body: Component type 37 runs the microprocessor update. It calls every input bridge, then the graph update with the embedded graph at +0x1c0, then every output bridge. Each bridge copies one value: an input bridge reads the connected vehicle signal into a graph node, and an output bridge writes a graph output to the connected signal. Bridges with no connection do nothing.

sections.title: Ports
sections.body: The definition lists no logic nodes and no tooltip. The ports come from the bridges of the embedded graph, with number, on/off, composite, video and audio bridge types. Read the ports from the microcontroller you placed, not from the definition.

sections.title: Composite, video and audio bridges
sections.body: A composite bridge copies the whole 132-byte value, the on/off mask and all 32 numbers, between the connected signal and its graph node, in both directions. A video bridge copies the fixed video descriptor field by field and allocates nothing. An audio bridge copies the samples into a buffer the receiving side owns. No bridge converts one kind into another: video and audio never enter composite channels.

sections.title: Size and port placement
sections.body: The editor's width and length controls run from 1 to 6 in steps of 1, and the upload check rejects a microcontroller whose width or length is above 6 with "Microcontroller must not be larger than 6x6 voxels". A port must sit inside the grid, 0 ≤ x < width and 0 ≤ z < length, in the bottom row y = 0. Two ports at one position are rejected when they have the same kind, or kinds 0 and 1 (internal codes); other kinds may share a position. The rule limits ports per position, not in total, and the 32 composite channels set no port limit.

sections.title: Port and graph counts
sections.body:
Add Input allocates a node, gives it the next ID from a 32-bit counter, creates its bridge with an ID from a second 32-bit counter, and appends the node to the port list. The list grows when it is full, and nothing compares the count with a maximum or checks the counters for overflow or duplicates. The upload check tests the size, that the graph and port lists are not empty, that an output exists and where each port sits, but not how many ports there are.

Limits depend on the path. A binary save reads the port list and each nested group list with a 16-bit count and reads the entries only for counts 1 to 32,768; a larger count skips that list. Component lists use 32-bit counts, XML import grows its lists as it reads them, and the graph update walks whatever its lists hold.

With the five bridged kinds at most 4 ports fit one position, one on/off or number port plus one composite, one video and one audio, so 144 on a 6 by 6 grid. That is a placement bound on the largest footprint, not a storage or execution limit.

sections.title: Composite channels inside the graph
sections.body: The composite read nodes (on/off and number) clamp their channel to 1 to 32, so channel 0 or less reads channel 1 and anything above 32 reads channel 32. A channel taken from an input is rounded first by adding 0.5 (inference: the library call is floor). Lua getBool and getNumber instead return false and 0 outside 1 to 32, setBool and setNumber ignore such channels, and setNumber rounds the Lua number to binary32. The Logic category gives the channel layout.

sections.title: Inside the graph
sections.body: The graph gathers every component's inputs before it runs any component, so a change moves one component per update (inference). Its components are separate routines from the physical gates: the PID has no max_error clamp, and the Blinker differs, as their part pages note.

families.summary: Supplies oxygen and the air throttle; air pressure in atmospheres boosts intake by up to two times.

sections.title: Performance drivers
sections.body: The cylinder averages the pressure of the pipe networks on its air manifolds' ports, in atmospheres, and multiplies intake by clamp(1 + 0.01 × pressure, 1, 2): 1.01 at 1 atm and 2 from 100 atm. Pressure is 60 × amount ÷ volume for a volume up to 8, the law the Tank Pressure output uses. Intake is capped by the oxygen in those manifolds.

sections.title: Air throttle
sections.body: Each air manifold clamps its input to 0 to 1. The group keeps the largest value among its air manifolds and hands it to the cylinders once per group update.

findings.label: Pressure-scaled intake coefficient
findings.detail: Intake term = RPS × this × listed-voxel count ÷ 60 × air throttle (group offset 0x90) × pressure factor, capped by the oxygen found in the connected air manifolds. Function 0x140449670-0x14044acc9; it reads binary32 2.8e-06 (bytes a2e73b36) at 0x140baf864. Interpretation rests on retained output investigation/native/behavior/pseudocode/0x140449670.c:L145,L213. findings.label: Compartment pressure law
findings.detail: All 13 fluid indices (0 to 12) enter only as liquid sum L or gas sum G, with A = L + G. Pure gas reduces to P = 60 × A ÷ V at any volume. Pure liquid in a volume up to 8 (80 L), such as a pipe network of 4, also gives 60 × A ÷ V. Pure liquid above volume 8 gives max(0.5 × A ÷ V, 7.5 × (A − V + 8)): under 0.5 atm until less than 8 (80 L) of room is left, then 7.5 atm per amount (per 75 L) up to 60 at full. Temperature does not enter. Inference from the instruction sequence; degenerate states follow the original SSE arithmetic. Report: investigation/fluids-network.md. Inputs: native:stormworks64.exe:f9206d85c82f:0x1402eb460@0x1402eb471, native:stormworks64.exe:f9206d85c82f:0x1402eb460@0x1402eb4b6, native:stormworks64.exe:f9206d85c82f:0x1402eb500@0x1402eb51b, native:stormworks64.exe:f9206d85c82f:0x1402eb500@0x1402eb539, native:stormworks64.exe:f9206d85c82f:0x1402eb550@0x1402eb550.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Charge per update is 0.05 × |w| × min(|w| ÷ 560, 0.25), with w its own RPS after belt mixing: quadratic up to 140 RPS, linear above.

sections.title: Performance drivers
sections.body: Case 5 adds electric_magnitude × force_emitter_max_force × 0.1 × 0.1 × |w| × min(|w| ÷ 560, 0.25) per update, with electric_magnitude 0.05 and force_emitter_max_force 100, so 0.05 × |w| × min(|w| ÷ 560, 0.25). The second factor saturates at |w| = 140, so the output is quadratic in speed below that and linear above it. The alternator then keeps (1 − min(|w| ÷ 560, 0.25)) of its speed, which is the load it puts on the belt. At 20 RPS it deposits 0.035714 per update, 2.1429 per simulated second.

sections.title: Belt coupling
sections.body: w is the alternator's own speed in RPS, in the crank's reference: the belt connects 1:1. Before charging, the alternator and crank mix by its Clutch Pressure u: r + J ÷ (I + J) × u × (w - r) and w + I ÷ (I + J) × u × (r - w), with J = 0.5. When damaged it deposits nothing but still drags. Charge goes into the electrical network's generation sum in native charge units.

families.summary: Coolant in the manifold exchanges heat with the engine group at k = 0.04 × liquid share × (1 - 0.8 × scaling)³ per update.

sections.title: Coolant exchange
sections.body: Each group update, for a nonempty coolant compartment, k = 0.04 × (liquid amount ÷ total amount) × (1 - 0.8 × scaling)³. The coolant moves k of the gap toward the engine, and the engine loses W × k × gap ÷ C, with W the fresh plus sea water amount and C = 1 + 40 × the group's cylinder voxels. Both changes use the temperatures from before the exchange. Clean, unscaled water gives k = 0.04; fully scaled water 0.00032. Gas in the compartment lowers k, and diesel, oil or slurry count as liquid without adding to W.

sections.title: Scaling
sections.body: Coolant Scaling grows by sea water amount × 1e-05 × clamp((engine °C - 100) ÷ 100, 0, 1) per update, up to 100 %. Fresh water does not scale and this update never removes scaling. Cylinder heat goes into the same group temperature that the overheat check at 115 °C reads, so circulating clean coolant through this manifold is the lever against damage.

families.summary: Belt-driven pump coupled to the crank by clutch pressure; its own speed decays by the factor 0.99 every update.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: The fluid-pump case couples the pump speed to the crank weighted by its engine_max_force (0.5) against the crank inertia, scaled by Clutch Pressure clamped between zero and one, then pumps and multiplies its speed by 0.99. Uncoupled, it keeps 0.547 of its speed after one simulated second (time constant 1.66 s).

sections.title: Flow
sections.body: The pump pushes with a bias equal to its own shaft speed in RPS and is one-way. At equal pressure it moves at most 20 L/s per RPS, reaching the 400 L/s bound at 20 RPS. Its speed is not crank RPS × clutch: it moves toward the belt speed by the clutch and inertia share each update and is then multiplied by 0.99. Without a belt group, or when damaged, it passes fluid only where pressure already pushes it. Its pump_pressure field is not read.

findings.label: Equal-pressure pump flow bound
findings.value: min(max(b, 0), 20) ÷ 30 per update; small 200 L/s, large 400 L/s; 400 L/s absolute
findings.detail: With pipe networks of volume 4 on both ports at equal pressure and away from empty or full states, demand = (P_A - P_B + 2 × b) ÷ 30 and the move is at most half of it, so q ≤ min(max(b, 0), 20) ÷ 30 amount per update. The ±20 target band caps every listed pump at 2 ÷ 3 amount per update, 400 L/s. Small electric pump at full power, b = 10: 1 ÷ 3 per update, 20 amount per second, 200 L/s. Large, b = 100: 2 ÷ 3, 40 amount per second, 400 L/s. A small pump can exceed 200 L/s when upstream pressure helps it. These are bounds, not the flow a loop delivers; fill, backpressure and competing ports reduce it. Report: investigation/fluid-transport.md. families.summary: Supplies diesel and the fuel throttle; fuel admission stops above 60 RPS.

sections.title: Performance drivers
sections.body: Fuel per update is RPS × 4e-6 × cylinder voxels × fuel throttle, capped by available diesel. Keep the fuel throttle about half of the air throttle without boost to stay inside the 12–16 window.

sections.title: Fuel throttle
sections.body: Each intake manifold clamps its input to 0 to 1. The group keeps the largest value among its intake manifolds and hands it to the cylinders once per group update; inputs are not summed.

families.summary: Pushes the crank only below 5 RPS, in proportion to the shortfall, while powered.

sections.title: Operating conditions
sections.body: Case 7 runs while the starter input is on and the component is undamaged. It draws electricity through the shared helper and adds speed proportional to (5 − crank RPS), clamped at zero. Its speed is coupled to the crank with weights engine_max_force (0.5) and the crank inertia, then decays by 0.99 per update. Without coupling or drive it would keep 0.547 of its speed after one simulated second.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Because assistance ends at 5 RPS and a cylinder needs more than 2 RPS plus a valid mixture, set the throttles before cranking. Large flywheels reduce how fast the starter can bring the crank up.

families.summary: Moving head of the Compact Robotic Pivot or Compact Velocity Pivot. Its base sets the motor.

sections.title: What drives it
sections.body: This is the moving half that Compact Robotic Pivot or Compact Velocity Pivot places as its child_name. The base runs the motor; this definition carries flag 0x80 without the powered bit, so its own motor fields do not set the joint's performance.

sections.title: Assembled joint
sections.body: With the Compact Robotic Pivot it is a position servo: Rotation Target sets an angle within ±0.25 turns. Gear Ratio divides its speed by r and the impulse cap is 200 × r² × P. With the Compact Velocity Pivot it is a speed motor: Rotational Speed s turns it at s × 5 ÷ r turns per second (at most 10), with impulse cap A × 100 × r² × P.

findings.label: Compact Pivot · flags
findings.detail: multibody_compact_pivot_b: definition attribute flags. Bit 0x80 marks a moving head; it lacks the powered bit 0x100.

findings.label: Compact Robotic Pivot · child_name
findings.detail: multibody_compact_pivot_robotic_a: definition attribute child_name. The base places this head.

findings.label: Compact Velocity Pivot · child_name
findings.detail: multibody_compact_pivot_velocity_a: definition attribute child_name. The base places this head.

findings.label: Compact Robotic Pivot rule
findings.value: θ = π × 0.5 × s rad; ω = clamp(10 × (θ − angle), −W, W) × 5 ÷ r rad/s; J = 200 × r² × P
findings.detail: multibody_compact_pivot_robotic_a: Limits ±1.5707963 rad = ±90 degrees = ±0.25 turns. limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Position servo: Rotation Target sets an angle within ±0.25 turns. Gear Ratio divides its speed by r and the impulse cap is 200 × r² × P.

sections.title: How it moves
sections.body: Rotation Target s (after smoothing) sets a target angle of π × 0.5 × s rad, ±90 degrees at s = ±1, and the setup puts hard stops at ±0.25 turns. Each update the motor aims for clamp(10 × angle error, −W, W) × 5 ÷ r rad/s, where W is the Speed setting (0.1 to 5, default 1). So it moves at up to W × 5 ÷ r rad/s and slows over the last W ÷ 10 rad.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is 200 × r² × P. With Max Power 100% it is 200 at 1:1, 800 at 1:2, 3200 at 1:4, 12800 at 1:8, 51200 at 1:16, 204800 at 1:32. Electrical availability does not lower the cap; it slows how fast the target follows the input. Each update requests 0.01 × |c| electricity, so a joint resting on its target requests none.

families.summary: Speed motor: Rotational Speed s turns it at s × 5 ÷ r turns per second (at most 10), with impulse cap A × 100 × r² × P.

sections.title: How it moves
sections.body: The command is clamp(s × 5 ÷ r, −10, 10) turns per second. At s = 1 that is 5 at 1:1, 2.5 at 1:2, 1.25 at 1:4, 0.625 at 1:8, 0.3125 at 1:16, 0.15625 at 1:32. There is no angle limit; the motor turns continuously.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is A × 100 × r² × P, where A is the electrical and damage availability. At A = P = 1 it is 100 at 1:1, 400 at 1:2, 1600 at 1:4, 6400 at 1:8, 25600 at 1:16, 102400 at 1:32. At s = 0 the motor stays on with this cap, so it brakes and holds. Each update requests about 0.1 × |ω| × P electricity, ω = 2π × turns per second.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Position servo: Rotation Target sets an angle within ±0.25 turns. Gear Ratio divides its speed by r and the impulse cap is 400 × r² × P.

sections.title: How it moves
sections.body: Rotation Target s (after smoothing) sets a target angle of π × 0.5 × s rad, ±90 degrees at s = ±1, and the setup puts hard stops at ±0.25 turns. Each update the motor aims for clamp(10 × angle error, −W, W) × 5 ÷ r rad/s, where W is the Speed setting (0.1 to 5, default 1). So it moves at up to W × 5 ÷ r rad/s and slows over the last W ÷ 10 rad.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is 400 × r² × P. With Max Power 100% it is 400 at 1:1, 1600 at 1:2, 6400 at 1:4, 25600 at 1:8, 102400 at 1:16, 409600 at 1:32. Electrical availability does not lower the cap; it slows how fast the target follows the input. Each update requests 0.01 × |c| electricity, so a joint resting on its target requests none.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Current Rotation reports σ × angle ÷ 2π in turns.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Moving head of the Robotic Door Hinge. Position servo: Rotation Target sets an angle within ±0.25 turns. Gear Ratio divides its speed by r and the impulse cap is 400 × r² × P.

sections.title: What drives it
sections.body: This is the moving half that Robotic Door Hinge places as its child_name. The base runs the motor; this definition carries flag 0x80 without the powered bit, so its own motor fields do not set the joint's performance.

sections.title: Assembled joint
sections.body: Position servo: Rotation Target sets an angle within ±0.25 turns. Gear Ratio divides its speed by r and the impulse cap is 400 × r² × P. Rotation Target s (after smoothing) sets a target angle of π × 0.5 × s rad, ±90 degrees at s = ±1, and the setup puts hard stops at ±0.25 turns. Each update the motor aims for clamp(10 × angle error, −W, W) × 5 ÷ r rad/s, where W is the Speed setting (0.1 to 5, default 1). So it moves at up to W × 5 ÷ r rad/s and slows over the last W ÷ 10 rad.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is 400 × r² × P. With Max Power 100% it is 400 at 1:1, 1600 at 1:2, 6400 at 1:4, 25600 at 1:8, 102400 at 1:16, 409600 at 1:32. Electrical availability does not lower the cap; it slows how fast the target follows the input. Each update requests 0.01 × |c| electricity, so a joint resting on its target requests none.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Slider over ±0.25 m driven at 1 m/s with a force cap of 100000 × P × |x + 0.5|, 25000 × P to 75000 × P across the travel.

sections.title: How it moves
sections.body: Each update the slider motor targets σ × 1 m/s along its axis (constraint_axis 1), with a force cap of 100000 × P × |x + 0.5| for slider position x in metres. Over the stops at ±0.25 m the cap rises from 25000 × P to 75000 × P. There is no separate spring rate or damping coefficient.

sections.title: Max Power
sections.body: Max Power runs from 1 to 100% and scales the cap. Gear Ratio, electricity and the max_motor_force field (1000) do not enter this branch.

families.summary: Moving head of the Piston Suspension. Slider over ±0.25 m driven at 1 m/s with a force cap of 100000 × P × |x + 0.5|, 25000 × P to 75000 × P across the travel.

sections.title: What drives it
sections.body: This is the moving half that Piston Suspension places as its child_name. The base runs the motor; this definition carries flag 0x80 without the powered bit, so its own motor fields do not set the joint's performance.

sections.title: Assembled joint
sections.body: Slider over ±0.25 m driven at 1 m/s with a force cap of 100000 × P × |x + 0.5|, 25000 × P to 75000 × P across the travel. Each update the slider motor targets σ × 1 m/s along its axis (constraint_axis 1), with a force cap of 100000 × P × |x + 0.5| for slider position x in metres. Over the stops at ±0.25 m the cap rises from 25000 × P to 75000 × P. There is no separate spring rate or damping coefficient.

sections.title: Max Power
sections.body: Max Power runs from 1 to 100% and scales the cap. Gear Ratio, electricity and the max_motor_force field (1000) do not enter this branch.

families.summary: Position servo: Rotation Target sets an angle within ±0.25 turns. Gear Ratio divides its speed by r and the impulse cap is 400 × r² × P.

sections.title: How it moves
sections.body: Rotation Target s (after smoothing) sets a target angle of π × 0.5 × s rad, ±90 degrees at s = ±1, and the setup puts hard stops at ±0.25 turns. Each update the motor aims for clamp(10 × angle error, −W, W) × 5 ÷ r rad/s, where W is the Speed setting (0.1 to 5, default 1). So it moves at up to W × 5 ÷ r rad/s and slows over the last W ÷ 10 rad.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is 400 × r² × P. With Max Power 100% it is 400 at 1:1, 1600 at 1:2, 6400 at 1:4, 25600 at 1:8, 102400 at 1:16, 409600 at 1:32. Electrical availability does not lower the cap; it slows how fast the target follows the input. Each update requests 0.01 × |c| electricity, so a joint resting on its target requests none.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The RPS port passes mechanical power across the joint. The Fluid port carries fluid across the joint through the shared two-port solver, both ways, all species, with no bias and flow factor 1, so the joint itself adds no restriction. Delivered flow still follows the pressures on both sides. The motor does not read that pressure. Current Rotation reports σ × angle ÷ 2π in turns.

findings.label: Robotic Hinge rule
findings.value: θ = π × 0.5 × s rad; ω = clamp(10 × (θ − angle), −W, W) × 5 ÷ r rad/s; J = 400 × r² × P
findings.detail: multibody_robotic_hinge_01_a: Limits ±1.5707963 rad = ±90 degrees = ±0.25 turns. limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Moving head of the Robotic Hinge. Position servo: Rotation Target sets an angle within ±0.25 turns. Gear Ratio divides its speed by r and the impulse cap is 400 × r² × P.

sections.title: What drives it
sections.body: This is the moving half that Robotic Hinge places as its child_name. The base runs the motor; this definition carries flag 0x80 without the powered bit, so its own motor fields do not set the joint's performance.

sections.title: Assembled joint
sections.body: Position servo: Rotation Target sets an angle within ±0.25 turns. Gear Ratio divides its speed by r and the impulse cap is 400 × r² × P. Rotation Target s (after smoothing) sets a target angle of π × 0.5 × s rad, ±90 degrees at s = ±1, and the setup puts hard stops at ±0.25 turns. Each update the motor aims for clamp(10 × angle error, −W, W) × 5 ÷ r rad/s, where W is the Speed setting (0.1 to 5, default 1). So it moves at up to W × 5 ÷ r rad/s and slows over the last W ÷ 10 rad.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is 400 × r² × P. With Max Power 100% it is 400 at 1:1, 1600 at 1:2, 6400 at 1:4, 25600 at 1:8, 102400 at 1:16, 409600 at 1:32. Electrical availability does not lower the cap; it slows how fast the target follows the input. Each update requests 0.01 × |c| electricity, so a joint resting on its target requests none.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The RPS port passes mechanical power across the joint. The Fluid port carries fluid across the joint through the shared two-port solver, both ways, all species, with no bias and flow factor 1, so the joint itself adds no restriction. Delivered flow still follows the pressures on both sides. The motor does not read that pressure.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Position servo: Rotation Target sets an angle within ±0.25 turns. Gear Ratio divides its speed by r and the impulse cap is 200 × r² × P.

sections.title: How it moves
sections.body: Rotation Target s (after smoothing) sets a target angle of π × 0.5 × s rad, ±90 degrees at s = ±1, and the setup puts hard stops at ±0.25 turns. Each update the motor aims for clamp(10 × angle error, −W, W) × 5 ÷ r rad/s, where W is the Speed setting (0.1 to 5, default 1). So it moves at up to W × 5 ÷ r rad/s and slows over the last W ÷ 10 rad.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is 200 × r² × P. With Max Power 100% it is 200 at 1:1, 800 at 1:2, 3200 at 1:4, 12800 at 1:8, 51200 at 1:16, 204800 at 1:32. Electrical availability does not lower the cap; it slows how fast the target follows the input. Each update requests 0.01 × |c| electricity, so a joint resting on its target requests none.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The RPS port passes mechanical power across the joint. Current Rotation reports σ × angle ÷ 2π in turns.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Position servo: Rotation Target sets an angle within ±0.25 turns. Gear Ratio divides its speed by r and the impulse cap is 200 × r² × P.

sections.title: How it moves
sections.body: Rotation Target s (after smoothing) sets a target angle of π × 0.5 × s rad, ±90 degrees at s = ±1, and the setup puts hard stops at ±0.25 turns. Each update the motor aims for clamp(10 × angle error, −W, W) × 5 ÷ r rad/s, where W is the Speed setting (0.1 to 5, default 1). So it moves at up to W × 5 ÷ r rad/s and slows over the last W ÷ 10 rad.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is 200 × r² × P. With Max Power 100% it is 200 at 1:1, 800 at 1:2, 3200 at 1:4, 12800 at 1:8, 51200 at 1:16, 204800 at 1:32. Electrical availability does not lower the cap; it slows how fast the target follows the input. Each update requests 0.01 × |c| electricity, so a joint resting on its target requests none.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The Fluid port carries fluid across the joint through the shared two-port solver, both ways, all species, with no bias and flow factor 1, so the joint itself adds no restriction. Delivered flow still follows the pressures on both sides. The motor does not read that pressure. Current Rotation reports σ × angle ÷ 2π in turns.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Moving head of the Robotic Pivot (Power). Position servo: Rotation Target sets an angle within ±0.25 turns. Gear Ratio divides its speed by r and the impulse cap is 200 × r² × P.

sections.title: What drives it
sections.body: This is the moving half that Robotic Pivot (Power) places as its child_name. The base runs the motor; this definition carries flag 0x80 without the powered bit, so its own motor fields do not set the joint's performance.

sections.title: Assembled joint
sections.body: Position servo: Rotation Target sets an angle within ±0.25 turns. Gear Ratio divides its speed by r and the impulse cap is 200 × r² × P. Rotation Target s (after smoothing) sets a target angle of π × 0.5 × s rad, ±90 degrees at s = ±1, and the setup puts hard stops at ±0.25 turns. Each update the motor aims for clamp(10 × angle error, −W, W) × 5 ÷ r rad/s, where W is the Speed setting (0.1 to 5, default 1). So it moves at up to W × 5 ÷ r rad/s and slows over the last W ÷ 10 rad.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is 200 × r² × P. With Max Power 100% it is 200 at 1:1, 800 at 1:2, 3200 at 1:4, 12800 at 1:8, 51200 at 1:16, 204800 at 1:32. Electrical availability does not lower the cap; it slows how fast the target follows the input. Each update requests 0.01 × |c| electricity, so a joint resting on its target requests none.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The RPS port passes mechanical power across the joint.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Moving head of the Robotic Pivot (Fluid). Position servo: Rotation Target sets an angle within ±0.25 turns. Gear Ratio divides its speed by r and the impulse cap is 200 × r² × P.

sections.title: What drives it
sections.body: This is the moving half that Robotic Pivot (Fluid) places as its child_name. The base runs the motor; this definition carries flag 0x80 without the powered bit, so its own motor fields do not set the joint's performance.

sections.title: Assembled joint
sections.body: Position servo: Rotation Target sets an angle within ±0.25 turns. Gear Ratio divides its speed by r and the impulse cap is 200 × r² × P. Rotation Target s (after smoothing) sets a target angle of π × 0.5 × s rad, ±90 degrees at s = ±1, and the setup puts hard stops at ±0.25 turns. Each update the motor aims for clamp(10 × angle error, −W, W) × 5 ÷ r rad/s, where W is the Speed setting (0.1 to 5, default 1). So it moves at up to W × 5 ÷ r rad/s and slows over the last W ÷ 10 rad.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is 200 × r² × P. With Max Power 100% it is 200 at 1:1, 800 at 1:2, 3200 at 1:4, 12800 at 1:8, 51200 at 1:16, 204800 at 1:32. Electrical availability does not lower the cap; it slows how fast the target follows the input. Each update requests 0.01 × |c| electricity, so a joint resting on its target requests none.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The Fluid port carries fluid across the joint through the shared two-port solver, both ways, all species, with no bias and flow factor 1, so the joint itself adds no restriction. Delivered flow still follows the pressures on both sides. The motor does not read that pressure.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Slider over ±0.25 m driven at 1 m/s with a force cap of 100000 × P × |x + 0.5|, 25000 × P to 75000 × P across the travel.

sections.title: How it moves
sections.body: Each update the slider motor targets −σ × 1 m/s along its axis (constraint_axis 0), with a force cap of 100000 × P × |x + 0.5| for slider position x in metres. Over the stops at ±0.25 m the cap rises from 25000 × P to 75000 × P. There is no separate spring rate or damping coefficient.

sections.title: Max Power
sections.body: Max Power runs from 1 to 100% and scales the cap. Gear Ratio, electricity and the max_motor_force field (1000) do not enter this branch.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The RPS port passes mechanical power across the joint.

families.summary: Moving head of the Suspension. Slider over ±0.25 m driven at 1 m/s with a force cap of 100000 × P × |x + 0.5|, 25000 × P to 75000 × P across the travel.

sections.title: What drives it
sections.body: This is the moving half that Suspension places as its child_name. The base runs the motor; this definition carries flag 0x80 without the powered bit, so its own motor fields do not set the joint's performance.

sections.title: Assembled joint
sections.body: Slider over ±0.25 m driven at 1 m/s with a force cap of 100000 × P × |x + 0.5|, 25000 × P to 75000 × P across the travel. Each update the slider motor targets −σ × 1 m/s along its axis (constraint_axis 0), with a force cap of 100000 × P × |x + 0.5| for slider position x in metres. Over the stops at ±0.25 m the cap rises from 25000 × P to 75000 × P. There is no separate spring rate or damping coefficient.

sections.title: Max Power
sections.body: Max Power runs from 1 to 100% and scales the cap. Gear Ratio, electricity and the max_motor_force field (1000) do not enter this branch.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The RPS port passes mechanical power across the joint.

families.summary: Speed motor: Rotational Speed s turns it at s × 0.5 ÷ r turns per second (at most 10), with impulse cap A × 2000 × r² × P.

sections.title: How it moves
sections.body: The command is clamp(s × 0.5 ÷ r, −10, 10) turns per second. At s = 1 that is 0.5 at 1:1, 0.25 at 1:2, 0.125 at 1:4, 0.0625 at 1:8, 0.03125 at 1:16, 0.015625 at 1:32. There is no angle limit; the motor turns continuously.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is A × 2000 × r² × P, where A is the electrical and damage availability. At A = P = 1 it is 2000 at 1:1, 8000 at 1:2, 32000 at 1:4, 128000 at 1:8, 512000 at 1:16, 2048000 at 1:32. At s = 0 the motor stays on with this cap, so it brakes and holds. Each update requests about 0.1 × |ω| × P electricity, ω = 2π × turns per second.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Current Rotation reports σ × angle ÷ 2π in turns, counted across full turns. The gap inside the ring forms a door seal, so a sealed compartment can continue through it.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: The three rings trade speed for capacity at a fixed product: small V 2 with F 500, medium V 1 with F 1000, large V 0.5 with F 2000. At 1:4 and full power they turn at 0.5, 0.25 and 0.125 turns per second with impulse caps 8000, 16000 and 32000.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Moving head of the Turret Ring (Large). Speed motor: Rotational Speed s turns it at s × 0.5 ÷ r turns per second (at most 10), with impulse cap A × 2000 × r² × P.

sections.title: What drives it
sections.body: This is the moving half that Turret Ring (Large) places as its child_name. The base runs the motor; this definition carries flag 0x80 without the powered bit, so its own motor fields do not set the joint's performance. Its name is Turret Ring (Large), but it is the head of the Turret Ring (Large).

sections.title: Assembled joint
sections.body: Speed motor: Rotational Speed s turns it at s × 0.5 ÷ r turns per second (at most 10), with impulse cap A × 2000 × r² × P. The command is clamp(s × 0.5 ÷ r, −10, 10) turns per second. At s = 1 that is 0.5 at 1:1, 0.25 at 1:2, 0.125 at 1:4, 0.0625 at 1:8, 0.03125 at 1:16, 0.015625 at 1:32. There is no angle limit; the motor turns continuously.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is A × 2000 × r² × P, where A is the electrical and damage availability. At A = P = 1 it is 2000 at 1:1, 8000 at 1:2, 32000 at 1:4, 128000 at 1:8, 512000 at 1:16, 2048000 at 1:32. At s = 0 the motor stays on with this cap, so it brakes and holds. Each update requests about 0.1 × |ω| × P electricity, ω = 2π × turns per second.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Speed motor: Rotational Speed s turns it at s × 1 ÷ r turns per second (at most 10), with impulse cap A × 1000 × r² × P.

sections.title: How it moves
sections.body: The command is clamp(s × 1 ÷ r, −10, 10) turns per second. At s = 1 that is 1 at 1:1, 0.5 at 1:2, 0.25 at 1:4, 0.125 at 1:8, 0.0625 at 1:16, 0.03125 at 1:32. There is no angle limit; the motor turns continuously.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is A × 1000 × r² × P, where A is the electrical and damage availability. At A = P = 1 it is 1000 at 1:1, 4000 at 1:2, 16000 at 1:4, 64000 at 1:8, 256000 at 1:16, 1024000 at 1:32. At s = 0 the motor stays on with this cap, so it brakes and holds. Each update requests about 0.1 × |ω| × P electricity, ω = 2π × turns per second.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Current Rotation reports σ × angle ÷ 2π in turns, counted across full turns. The gap inside the ring forms a door seal, so a sealed compartment can continue through it.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: The three rings trade speed for capacity at a fixed product: small V 2 with F 500, medium V 1 with F 1000, large V 0.5 with F 2000. At 1:4 and full power they turn at 0.5, 0.25 and 0.125 turns per second with impulse caps 8000, 16000 and 32000.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Moving head of the Turret Ring (Medium). Speed motor: Rotational Speed s turns it at s × 1 ÷ r turns per second (at most 10), with impulse cap A × 1000 × r² × P.

sections.title: What drives it
sections.body: This is the moving half that Turret Ring (Medium) places as its child_name. The base runs the motor; this definition carries flag 0x80 without the powered bit, so its own motor fields do not set the joint's performance. Its name is Turret Ring (Medium), but it is the head of the Turret Ring (Medium).

sections.title: Assembled joint
sections.body: Speed motor: Rotational Speed s turns it at s × 1 ÷ r turns per second (at most 10), with impulse cap A × 1000 × r² × P. The command is clamp(s × 1 ÷ r, −10, 10) turns per second. At s = 1 that is 1 at 1:1, 0.5 at 1:2, 0.25 at 1:4, 0.125 at 1:8, 0.0625 at 1:16, 0.03125 at 1:32. There is no angle limit; the motor turns continuously.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is A × 1000 × r² × P, where A is the electrical and damage availability. At A = P = 1 it is 1000 at 1:1, 4000 at 1:2, 16000 at 1:4, 64000 at 1:8, 256000 at 1:16, 1024000 at 1:32. At s = 0 the motor stays on with this cap, so it brakes and holds. Each update requests about 0.1 × |ω| × P electricity, ω = 2π × turns per second.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Speed motor: Rotational Speed s turns it at s × 2 ÷ r turns per second (at most 10), with impulse cap A × 500 × r² × P.

sections.title: How it moves
sections.body: The command is clamp(s × 2 ÷ r, −10, 10) turns per second. At s = 1 that is 2 at 1:1, 1 at 1:2, 0.5 at 1:4, 0.25 at 1:8, 0.125 at 1:16, 0.0625 at 1:32. There is no angle limit; the motor turns continuously.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is A × 500 × r² × P, where A is the electrical and damage availability. At A = P = 1 it is 500 at 1:1, 2000 at 1:2, 8000 at 1:4, 32000 at 1:8, 128000 at 1:16, 512000 at 1:32. At s = 0 the motor stays on with this cap, so it brakes and holds. Each update requests about 0.1 × |ω| × P electricity, ω = 2π × turns per second.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Current Rotation reports σ × angle ÷ 2π in turns, counted across full turns. The gap inside the ring forms a door seal, so a sealed compartment can continue through it.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: The three rings trade speed for capacity at a fixed product: small V 2 with F 500, medium V 1 with F 1000, large V 0.5 with F 2000. At 1:4 and full power they turn at 0.5, 0.25 and 0.125 turns per second with impulse caps 8000, 16000 and 32000.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Moving head of the Turret Ring (Small). Speed motor: Rotational Speed s turns it at s × 2 ÷ r turns per second (at most 10), with impulse cap A × 500 × r² × P.

sections.title: What drives it
sections.body: This is the moving half that Turret Ring (Small) places as its child_name. The base runs the motor; this definition carries flag 0x80 without the powered bit, so its own motor fields do not set the joint's performance. Its name is Turret Ring (Small), but it is the head of the Turret Ring (Small).

sections.title: Assembled joint
sections.body: Speed motor: Rotational Speed s turns it at s × 2 ÷ r turns per second (at most 10), with impulse cap A × 500 × r² × P. The command is clamp(s × 2 ÷ r, −10, 10) turns per second. At s = 1 that is 2 at 1:1, 1 at 1:2, 0.5 at 1:4, 0.25 at 1:8, 0.125 at 1:16, 0.0625 at 1:32. There is no angle limit; the motor turns continuously.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is A × 500 × r² × P, where A is the electrical and damage availability. At A = P = 1 it is 500 at 1:1, 2000 at 1:2, 8000 at 1:4, 32000 at 1:8, 128000 at 1:16, 512000 at 1:32. At s = 0 the motor stays on with this cap, so it brakes and holds. Each update requests about 0.1 × |ω| × P electricity, ω = 2π × turns per second.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Speed motor: Rotational Speed s turns it at s × 5 ÷ r turns per second (at most 10), with impulse cap A × 1000 × r² × P.

sections.title: How it moves
sections.body: The command is clamp(s × 5 ÷ r, −10, 10) turns per second. At s = 1 that is 5 at 1:1, 2.5 at 1:2, 1.25 at 1:4, 0.625 at 1:8, 0.3125 at 1:16, 0.15625 at 1:32. There is no angle limit; the motor turns continuously.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is A × 1000 × r² × P, where A is the electrical and damage availability. At A = P = 1 it is 1000 at 1:1, 4000 at 1:2, 16000 at 1:4, 64000 at 1:8, 256000 at 1:16, 1024000 at 1:32. At s = 0 the motor stays on with this cap, so it brakes and holds. Each update requests about 0.1 × |ω| × P electricity, ω = 2π × turns per second.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The Fluid port carries fluid across the joint through the shared two-port solver, both ways, all species, with no bias and flow factor 1, so the joint itself adds no restriction. Delivered flow still follows the pressures on both sides. The motor does not read that pressure. Current Rotation reports σ × angle ÷ 2π in turns, counted across full turns.

findings.label: Ticks per simulated second
findings.detail: The worker converts its tick count (worker+0xd0, loaded at 0x1405e3ad7) to binary32 and divides it by this, then passes the widened result as the elapsed time to the physics world's stepSimulation slot +0x60 at 0x1405e3b16, with at most 1000 solver substeps. findings.detail: The substep is 1 ÷ the worker's solver rate (worker+0xb8), or binary32 1/60 from 0x140baf98c in the fallback branch at 0x1405e3af4. limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Speed motor: Rotational Speed s turns it at s × 5 ÷ r turns per second (at most 10), with impulse cap A × 1000 × r² × P.

sections.title: How it moves
sections.body: The command is clamp(s × 5 ÷ r, −10, 10) turns per second. At s = 1 that is 5 at 1:1, 2.5 at 1:2, 1.25 at 1:4, 0.625 at 1:8, 0.3125 at 1:16, 0.15625 at 1:32. There is no angle limit; the motor turns continuously.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is A × 1000 × r² × P, where A is the electrical and damage availability. At A = P = 1 it is 1000 at 1:1, 4000 at 1:2, 16000 at 1:4, 64000 at 1:8, 256000 at 1:16, 1024000 at 1:32. At s = 0 the motor stays on with this cap, so it brakes and holds. Each update requests about 0.1 × |ω| × P electricity, ω = 2π × turns per second.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The RPS port passes mechanical power across the joint. Current Rotation reports σ × angle ÷ 2π in turns, counted across full turns.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Moving head of the Velocity Pivot (Fluid). Speed motor: Rotational Speed s turns it at s × 5 ÷ r turns per second (at most 10), with impulse cap A × 1000 × r² × P.

sections.title: What drives it
sections.body: This is the moving half that Velocity Pivot (Fluid) places as its child_name. The base runs the motor; this definition carries flag 0x80 without the powered bit, so its own motor fields do not set the joint's performance.

sections.title: Assembled joint
sections.body: Speed motor: Rotational Speed s turns it at s × 5 ÷ r turns per second (at most 10), with impulse cap A × 1000 × r² × P. The command is clamp(s × 5 ÷ r, −10, 10) turns per second. At s = 1 that is 5 at 1:1, 2.5 at 1:2, 1.25 at 1:4, 0.625 at 1:8, 0.3125 at 1:16, 0.15625 at 1:32. There is no angle limit; the motor turns continuously.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is A × 1000 × r² × P, where A is the electrical and damage availability. At A = P = 1 it is 1000 at 1:1, 4000 at 1:2, 16000 at 1:4, 64000 at 1:8, 256000 at 1:16, 1024000 at 1:32. At s = 0 the motor stays on with this cap, so it brakes and holds. Each update requests about 0.1 × |ω| × P electricity, ω = 2π × turns per second.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The Fluid port carries fluid across the joint through the shared two-port solver, both ways, all species, with no bias and flow factor 1, so the joint itself adds no restriction. Delivered flow still follows the pressures on both sides. The motor does not read that pressure.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Moving head of the Velocity Pivot (Power). Speed motor: Rotational Speed s turns it at s × 5 ÷ r turns per second (at most 10), with impulse cap A × 1000 × r² × P.

sections.title: What drives it
sections.body: This is the moving half that Velocity Pivot (Power) places as its child_name. The base runs the motor; this definition carries flag 0x80 without the powered bit, so its own motor fields do not set the joint's performance.

sections.title: Assembled joint
sections.body: Speed motor: Rotational Speed s turns it at s × 5 ÷ r turns per second (at most 10), with impulse cap A × 1000 × r² × P. The command is clamp(s × 5 ÷ r, −10, 10) turns per second. At s = 1 that is 5 at 1:1, 2.5 at 1:2, 1.25 at 1:4, 0.625 at 1:8, 0.3125 at 1:16, 0.15625 at 1:32. There is no angle limit; the motor turns continuously.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is A × 1000 × r² × P, where A is the electrical and damage availability. At A = P = 1 it is 1000 at 1:1, 4000 at 1:2, 16000 at 1:4, 64000 at 1:8, 256000 at 1:16, 1024000 at 1:32. At s = 0 the motor stays on with this cap, so it brakes and holds. Each update requests about 0.1 × |ω| × P electricity, ω = 2π × turns per second.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: The RPS port passes mechanical power across the joint.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Speed motor: Rotational Speed s turns it at s × 5 ÷ r turns per second (at most 10), with impulse cap A × 1000 × r² × P.

sections.title: How it moves
sections.body: The command is clamp(s × 5 ÷ r, −10, 10) turns per second. At s = 1 that is 5 at 1:1, 2.5 at 1:2, 1.25 at 1:4, 0.625 at 1:8, 0.3125 at 1:16, 0.15625 at 1:32. There is no angle limit; the motor turns continuously.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is A × 1000 × r² × P, where A is the electrical and damage availability. At A = P = 1 it is 1000 at 1:1, 4000 at 1:2, 16000 at 1:4, 64000 at 1:8, 256000 at 1:16, 1024000 at 1:32. At s = 0 the motor stays on with this cap, so it brakes and holds. Each update requests about 0.1 × |ω| × P electricity, ω = 2π × turns per second.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Current Rotation reports σ × angle ÷ 2π in turns, counted across full turns.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Moving head of the Velocity Pivot. Speed motor: Rotational Speed s turns it at s × 5 ÷ r turns per second (at most 10), with impulse cap A × 1000 × r² × P.

sections.title: What drives it
sections.body: This is the moving half that Velocity Pivot places as its child_name. The base runs the motor; this definition carries flag 0x80 without the powered bit, so its own motor fields do not set the joint's performance. Its name is Robotic Pivot, but it is the head of the Velocity Pivot.

sections.title: Assembled joint
sections.body: Speed motor: Rotational Speed s turns it at s × 5 ÷ r turns per second (at most 10), with impulse cap A × 1000 × r² × P. The command is clamp(s × 5 ÷ r, −10, 10) turns per second. At s = 1 that is 5 at 1:1, 2.5 at 1:2, 1.25 at 1:4, 0.625 at 1:8, 0.3125 at 1:16, 0.15625 at 1:32. There is no angle limit; the motor turns continuously.

sections.title: Gear Ratio and Max Power
sections.body: The impulse cap per physics step is A × 1000 × r² × P, where A is the electrical and damage availability. At A = P = 1 it is 1000 at 1:1, 4000 at 1:2, 16000 at 1:4, 64000 at 1:8, 256000 at 1:16, 1024000 at 1:32. At s = 0 the motor stays on with this cap, so it brakes and holds. Each update requests about 0.1 × |ω| × P electricity, ω = 2π × turns per second.

limitations: For active, normally simulated vehicles, these formulas run once per nominal 1/60-second simulation update. Multiply per-update amounts by 60 for amounts per simulated second. A constant relaxation fraction k leaves (1-k)^60 of a gap after one simulated second. Physics solver substeps and render frames are separate; pauses, sleeping, unloaded vehicles and real-time slowdown are outside this conversion.

families.summary: Pumps crude from a finite well buffer out of Fluid Out when a mechanical force cycles its piston, Oil Rig Pumpjack B: the piston sets a chamber of volume 10 × its travel fraction, and a pump_pressure bias of 10000 pushes the excess out.

sections.title: Piston
sections.body: The pumpjack names Oil Rig Pumpjack B as its child_name. The piston's own update does nothing (definition flag 0x80), so all pumping runs through this part and its Fluid Out port.

sections.title: Pump chamber
sections.body: Each update the pumpjack reads the piston's displacement x, its travel range r and the sign s of its mirrored axis, and forms the travel fraction u = clamp((s × x + r ÷ 2) ÷ r, 0, 1). It sets the chamber's volume to V = 10 × u, 100 L at full travel. With A the amount already in the chamber, the exchange factor is h = clamp(A − V, 0, 1): fluid leaves only while the chamber holds more than its volume, as when the piston compresses a filled chamber. This step changes the chamber's size and adds no crude.

sections.title: Outflow
sections.body: The pumpjack calls the port solver between Fluid Out and the chamber with bias pump_pressure, 10000, factor h and all species, allowing only flow from the chamber to the port. The solver's signed difference is d = P_port − P_chamber − 10000, so the bias pushes crude out against outlet pressure. It is a pressure bias in the transfer, not a rupture pressure or an outlet ceiling. The delivered amount still depends on the solver, the pressures on both sides and h.

sections.title: Well supply
sections.body: A separate branch tops the piston up from the well buffer: q = min(10 × u − A, buffer crude). A positive q moves that crude from the buffer into the piston, so the pumpjack draws a finite supply rather than creating oil. The buffer refills from an oil deposit by q = min(free buffer room × 0.05, deposit remaining), and the deposit loses what it gives. The deposit used is the non-empty one with the most remaining crude whose region contains the sampling point.

families.summary: Legacy radar: a target passes when its physics-body mass S over distance exceeds 0.25 (d < 4 × S), up to a far plane about 3875 m ahead at the default saved FOV. FOV input 0.01 to 0.125 turns.

sections.title: Detection
sections.body:
Logic case 50 scores each candidate as S ÷ d, with S the target's physics-body mass and d the straight-line distance, and requires more than 0.25, so d < 4 × S. radar_range does not enter the score. It sets the far plane C = P × (0.75 + 0.25 × 0.01 ÷ saved radar_fov) instead: with P = 5000 and the saved default 0.1, C is about 3875 m.

On the sensor's axis a target passes within min(3875, 4 × S) m: 40 m for S = 10, 400 m for S = 100, 3875 m for S = 1000. Off the axis the straight-line distance can exceed C. The target must also lie inside four side planes set by the FOV. Candidates go best score first through a line-of-sight query, and the first that passes is output.

sections.title: Field of view and aim
sections.body: The FOV input is clamped to 0.01 to 0.125 turn, 3.6 to 45 degrees horizontally; the vertical field is fixed at 0.25 turn, 90 degrees. Facing Yaw is clamped to -0.5 to 0.5 turn. Changing the FOV moves the side planes only: the far plane follows the saved radar_fov field, default 0.1.

sections.title: Height gates
sections.body: The radar runs only while its position is at least 0.25 m above a sampled height, and it sees only targets whose highest point is above y = 1. Reading that height as the water surface is an inference.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Outputs give distance in metres and angles in turns. They carry no SDK noise: radar_noise, radar_distance_noise and sonar_noise do not reach this logic case.

limitations: Far-plane figures assume the saved radar_fov default 0.1 and a target on the sensor's axis. S is read per physics body. Mass accounting, the height sampler, blocking materials and other saved radar_fov values are open questions listed under Other components.

families.summary: Range 60000 m at the default FOV, 240000 m to 384 m across the FOV sliders; a new scan every 30 updates (0.5 s); targets of body mass S pass out to 240 × S m at the default FOV.

sections.title: Detection
sections.body:
R = 60000 × 0.02 × 0.02 ÷ (FOV x × FOV y) m. The editor sliders set each axis from 0.01 to 0.25 in steps of 0.01: R is 240000 m at 0.01 per axis, 60000 m at the default 0.02 and 384 m at 0.25. A target of physics-body mass S at distance d passes when d ≤ R and R ÷ 10000 × S ÷ d > 0.025, that is d < R × S ÷ 250: 960 × S m at 0.01, 240 × S m at the default and 1.536 × S m at 0.25. Narrowing the FOV reaches farther but scans less often.

A new scan runs every max(1, floor(R ÷ 2000 + 0.5)) updates: 120 (2 s) at 0.01, 30 (0.5 s) at the default FOV and 1 (0.016667 s) at 0.25. Each scan keeps at most 8 targets, best score first, and checks line of sight to each.

sections.title: Outputs
sections.body: Angles are in turns. At the SDK defaults, distances carry up to ±1% noise and each angle up to ±0.001 turn (±0.36 degrees). The error is spread evenly over 32768 steps across that band, not bell-shaped.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: The tooltip gives no range, but radar_range is 60000. On the basic radars and sonars this field equals the stated range.

findings.label: Sensor noise distribution
findings.value: 32768 equally spaced values from −1 to 1, uniform over a full cycle
findings.detail: The advanced sensors form U = result ÷ 32767 and use 2U − 1, so the noise variable takes 32768 equally spaced values including −1 and 1. Inference: the generator has full period 2^32 (odd increment, multiplier 1 modulo 4), so over one cycle each 15-bit output occurs 2^17 times. The spread is uniform, not Gaussian, and draws are a fixed sequence from the seed, not independent samples. Report: investigation/leftovers.md. Inputs: native:stormworks64.exe:f9206d85c82f:0x1409afa20@0x1409afa29, native:stormworks64.exe:f9206d85c82f:0x1409afa20@0x1409afa30, native:stormworks64.exe:f9206d85c82f:0x1409afa20@0x1409afa39.

families.summary: Range 500000 m at the default FOV, 2000000 m to 3200 m across the FOV sliders; a new scan every 250 updates (4.166667 s); targets of body mass S pass out to 2000 × S m at the default FOV.

sections.title: Detection
sections.body:
R = 500000 × 0.02 × 0.02 ÷ (FOV x × FOV y) m. The editor sliders set each axis from 0.01 to 0.25 in steps of 0.01: R is 2000000 m at 0.01 per axis, 500000 m at the default 0.02 and 3200 m at 0.25. A target of physics-body mass S at distance d passes when d ≤ R and R ÷ 10000 × S ÷ d > 0.025, that is d < R × S ÷ 250: 8000 × S m at 0.01, 2000 × S m at the default and 12.8 × S m at 0.25. Narrowing the FOV reaches farther but scans less often.

A new scan runs every max(1, floor(R ÷ 2000 + 0.5)) updates: 1000 (16.666667 s) at 0.01, 250 (4.166667 s) at the default FOV and 2 (0.033333 s) at 0.25. Each scan keeps at most 8 targets, best score first, and checks line of sight to each.

sections.title: Outputs
sections.body: Angles are in turns. At the SDK defaults, distances carry up to ±1% noise and each angle up to ±0.001 turn (±0.36 degrees). The error is spread evenly over 32768 steps across that band, not bell-shaped.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: The tooltip gives no range, but radar_range is 500000. On the basic radars and sonars this field equals the stated range.

findings.label: Sensor noise distribution
findings.value: 32768 equally spaced values from −1 to 1, uniform over a full cycle
findings.detail: The advanced sensors form U = result ÷ 32767 and use 2U − 1, so the noise variable takes 32768 equally spaced values including −1 and 1. Inference: the generator has full period 2^32 (odd increment, multiplier 1 modulo 4), so over one cycle each 15-bit output occurs 2^17 times. The spread is uniform, not Gaussian, and draws are a fixed sequence from the seed, not independent samples. Report: investigation/leftovers.md. families.summary: Range 200000 m at the default FOV, 800000 m to 1280 m across the FOV sliders; a new scan every 100 updates (1.666667 s); targets of body mass S pass out to 800 × S m at the default FOV.

sections.title: Detection
sections.body:
R = 200000 × 0.02 × 0.02 ÷ (FOV x × FOV y) m. The editor sliders set each axis from 0.01 to 0.25 in steps of 0.01: R is 800000 m at 0.01 per axis, 200000 m at the default 0.02 and 1280 m at 0.25. A target of physics-body mass S at distance d passes when d ≤ R and R ÷ 10000 × S ÷ d > 0.025, that is d < R × S ÷ 250: 3200 × S m at 0.01, 800 × S m at the default and 5.12 × S m at 0.25. Narrowing the FOV reaches farther but scans less often.

A new scan runs every max(1, floor(R ÷ 2000 + 0.5)) updates: 400 (6.666667 s) at 0.01, 100 (1.666667 s) at the default FOV and 1 (0.016667 s) at 0.25. Each scan keeps at most 8 targets, best score first, and checks line of sight to each.

sections.title: Outputs
sections.body: Angles are in turns. At the SDK defaults, distances carry up to ±1% noise and each angle up to ±0.001 turn (±0.36 degrees). The error is spread evenly over 32768 steps across that band, not bell-shaped.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: The tooltip gives no range, but radar_range is 200000. On the basic radars and sonars this field equals the stated range.

findings.label: Sensor noise distribution
findings.value: 32768 equally spaced values from −1 to 1, uniform over a full cycle
findings.detail: The advanced sensors form U = result ÷ 32767 and use 2U − 1, so the noise variable takes 32768 equally spaced values including −1 and 1. Inference: the generator has full period 2^32 (odd increment, multiplier 1 modulo 4), so over one cycle each 15-bit output occurs 2^17 times. The spread is uniform, not Gaussian, and draws are a fixed sequence from the seed, not independent samples. Report: investigation/leftovers.md. families.summary: Range 20000 m at the default FOV, 80000 m to 128 m across the FOV sliders; a new scan every 10 updates (0.166667 s); targets of body mass S pass out to 80 × S m at the default FOV.

sections.title: Detection
sections.body:
R = 20000 × 0.02 × 0.02 ÷ (FOV x × FOV y) m. The editor sliders set each axis from 0.01 to 0.25 in steps of 0.01: R is 80000 m at 0.01 per axis, 20000 m at the default 0.02 and 128 m at 0.25. A target of physics-body mass S at distance d passes when d ≤ R and R ÷ 10000 × S ÷ d > 0.025, that is d < R × S ÷ 250: 320 × S m at 0.01, 80 × S m at the default and 0.512 × S m at 0.25. Narrowing the FOV reaches farther but scans less often.

A new scan runs every max(1, floor(R ÷ 2000 + 0.5)) updates: 40 (0.666667 s) at 0.01, 10 (0.166667 s) at the default FOV and 1 (0.016667 s) at 0.25. Each scan keeps at most 8 targets, best score first, and checks line of sight to each.

sections.title: Outputs
sections.body: Angles are in turns. At the SDK defaults, distances carry up to ±1% noise and each angle up to ±0.001 turn (±0.36 degrees). The error is spread evenly over 32768 steps across that band, not bell-shaped.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: The tooltip gives no range, but radar_range is 20000. On the basic radars and sonars this field equals the stated range.

sections.title: Scan frame and planes
sections.body:
Let R0, R1 and R2 be the rows of the part's world transform as the game stores them, and O its position. radar_type 1 sweeps them into M = A × B × R: B turns the first two rows by the negated sweep field at +0x468, then A turns the second and third rows by −2π × the field at +0x420. With X, Y and Z the rows of M, the radar looks along Y. The other advanced radars build their sweep in a different plane.

A target must lie strictly inside five planes: a far plane facing −Y at O + range × Y, and four side planes through O with normals ±cos(hy) X + sin(hy) Y and sin(hx) Y ∓ cos(hx) Z, where hy = π × FOV y and hx = π × FOV x. A target exactly on a plane fails. A separate check keeps it within range of O; it is a sphere, not a sixth plane. From the plane normals, FOV y sets the spread toward ±X and FOV x the spread toward ±Z, each a full width of FOV turns.

sections.title: Angles
sections.body:
Reported angles do not use the swept frame. They use right R0, forward R1 and up −R2 of the unswept transform: azimuth = atan2(u · R0, u · R1) ÷ 2π and elevation = asin(−u · R2) ÷ 2π, in turns, for the unit direction u to the target. Positive azimuth points toward R0 and positive elevation toward −R2. At zero scan angles the radar looks along R1. Because right × forward = −up, the output axes are mirrored relative to the R basis. A target straight behind reads +0.5 turn.

In the editor the part's straight arrow points along its mesh +Y, which is R1, so the arrow shows the radar's forward direction. R0 is the side axis and R2 the top axis, and positive elevation points toward −R2.

findings.label: Sensor noise distribution
findings.value: 32768 equally spaced values from −1 to 1, uniform over a full cycle
findings.detail: The advanced sensors form U = result ÷ 32767 and use 2U − 1, so the noise variable takes 32768 equally spaced values including −1 and 1. Inference: the generator has full period 2^32 (odd increment, multiplier 1 modulo 4), so over one cycle each 15-bit output occurs 2^17 times. The spread is uniform, not Gaussian, and draws are a fixed sequence from the seed, not independent samples. Report: investigation/leftovers.md. findings.label: Missile radar output axes
findings.detail: The radar_type 1 branch at 0x1403bb16e takes its output axes from the unswept transform: right R0, forward R1, up −R2. For a unit direction u the azimuth is atan2(u · R0, u · R1) ÷ 2π and the elevation asin(−u · R2) ÷ 2π, in turns. Positive azimuth points toward R0 and positive elevation toward −R2. right × forward = −up, so these axes have the opposite handedness to the R basis. limitations: S is the target's physics-body mass, read per physics body; how vehicle mass accounting and the environment shape it are open questions listed under Other components.

Range, score, scan interval and FOV slider limits match the other advanced radars. The axis assignment comes from the shipped arrow mesh and the native angle code; no angle was checked in a running game.
20000 is also the definition serializer's fallback for radar_range (it appears on hundreds of unrelated parts), so this value may be a default rather than a tuned range.

families.summary: Range 100000 m at the default FOV, 400000 m to 640 m across the FOV sliders; a new scan every 50 updates (0.833333 s); targets of body mass S pass out to 400 × S m at the default FOV.

sections.title: Detection
sections.body:
R = 100000 × 0.02 × 0.02 ÷ (FOV x × FOV y) m. The editor sliders set each axis from 0.01 to 0.25 in steps of 0.01: R is 400000 m at 0.01 per axis, 100000 m at the default 0.02 and 640 m at 0.25. A target of physics-body mass S at distance d passes when d ≤ R and R ÷ 10000 × S ÷ d > 0.025, that is d < R × S ÷ 250: 1600 × S m at 0.01, 400 × S m at the default and 2.56 × S m at 0.25. Narrowing the FOV reaches farther but scans less often.

A new scan runs every max(1, floor(R ÷ 2000 + 0.5)) updates: 200 (3.333333 s) at 0.01, 50 (0.833333 s) at the default FOV and 1 (0.016667 s) at 0.25. Each scan keeps at most 8 targets, best score first, and checks line of sight to each.

sections.title: Outputs
sections.body: Angles are in turns. At the SDK defaults, distances carry up to ±1% noise and each angle up to ±0.001 turn (±0.36 degrees). The error is spread evenly over 32768 steps across that band, not bell-shaped.

sections.title: Variant tradeoffs
sections.body: The tooltip gives no range, but radar_range is 100000. On the basic radars and sonars this field equals the stated range.

families.summary: Legacy radar: a target passes when its physics-body mass S over distance exceeds 0.25 (d < 4 × S), up to a far plane about 15500 m ahead at the default saved FOV. FOV input 0.01 to 0.125 turns.

sections.title: Detection
sections.body:
Logic case 50 scores each candidate as S ÷ d, with S the target's physics-body mass and d the straight-line distance, and requires more than 0.25, so d < 4 × S. radar_range does not enter the score. It sets the far plane C = P × (0.75 + 0.25 × 0.01 ÷ saved radar_fov) instead: with P = 20000 and the saved default 0.1, C is about 15500 m.

On the sensor's axis a target passes within min(15500, 4 × S) m: 40 m for S = 10, 400 m for S = 100, 4000 m for S = 1000. Off the axis the straight-line distance can exceed C. The target must also lie inside four side planes set by the FOV. Candidates go best score first through a line-of-sight query, and the first that passes is output.

sections.title: Field of view and aim
sections.body: The FOV input is clamped to 0.01 to 0.125 turn, 3.6 to 45 degrees horizontally; the vertical field is fixed at 0.25 turn, 90 degrees. This part has no Facing Yaw input. Changing the FOV moves the side planes only: the far plane follows the saved radar_fov field, default 0.1.

sections.title: Height gates
sections.body: The radar runs only while its position is at least 0.25 m above a sampled height, and it sees only targets whose highest point is above y = 1. Reading that height as the water surface is an inference.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Outputs give distance in metres and angles in turns. They carry no SDK noise: radar_noise, radar_distance_noise and sonar_noise do not reach this logic case.

findings.label: Radar (Dish) detection figures
findings.value: far plane C = 15500 m at saved radar_fov 0.1; on axis distance < min(15500, 4 × S)
findings.detail: P = 20000. C = 20000 × (0.75 + 0.25 × 0.01 ÷ 0.1) = 20000 × 0.775 = 15500 m. The score S ÷ d > 0.25 gives d < 4 × S. limitations: Far-plane figures assume the saved radar_fov default 0.1 and a target on the sensor's axis. S is read per physics body. Mass accounting, the height sampler, blocking materials and other saved radar_fov values are open questions listed under Other components.

families.summary: Legacy radar: a target passes when its physics-body mass S over distance exceeds 0.25 (d < 4 × S), up to a far plane about 38750 m ahead at the default saved FOV. FOV input 0.01 to 0.125 turns.

sections.title: Detection
sections.body:
Logic case 50 scores each candidate as S ÷ d, with S the target's physics-body mass and d the straight-line distance, and requires more than 0.25, so d < 4 × S. radar_range does not enter the score. It sets the far plane C = P × (0.75 + 0.25 × 0.01 ÷ saved radar_fov) instead: with P = 50000 and the saved default 0.1, C is about 38750 m.

On the sensor's axis a target passes within min(38750, 4 × S) m: 40 m for S = 10, 400 m for S = 100, 4000 m for S = 1000. Off the axis the straight-line distance can exceed C. The target must also lie inside four side planes set by the FOV. Up to 8 candidates that pass the line-of-sight query fill the Radar Data composite, best score first.

sections.title: Field of view and aim
sections.body: The FOV input is clamped to 0.01 to 0.125 turn, 3.6 to 45 degrees horizontally; the vertical field is fixed at 0.25 turn, 90 degrees. Facing Yaw is clamped to -0.5 to 0.5 turn. Changing the FOV moves the side planes only: the far plane follows the saved radar_fov field, default 0.1.

sections.title: Height gates
sections.body: The radar runs only while its position is at least 0.25 m above a sampled height, and it sees only targets whose highest point is above y = 1. Reading that height as the water surface is an inference.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Outputs give distance in metres and angles in turns. They carry no SDK noise: radar_noise, radar_distance_noise and sonar_noise do not reach this logic case. The Radar Data composite carries target 1 to 8 found flags and distance, azimuth, elevation and time since detection per target.

findings.label: Legacy sensor candidate call
findings.detail: Logic case 50 (jump-table entry 50 leads to 0x1403c6f4d) runs the legacy radars and sonars. It calls the candidate helper six times (0x1403c76ab to 0x1403c77e5), once per scene-object list, with five bounding planes. The helper requires a positive S, skips the sensor's own and several special records and requires the target strictly inside all five planes. No scan counter precedes these calls in the case-50 block (inference: candidates are collected on every update that passes the gates). Report: investigation/sensors-legacy.md. limitations: Far-plane figures assume the saved radar_fov default 0.1 and a target on the sensor's axis. S is read per physics body. Mass accounting, the height sampler, blocking materials and other saved radar_fov values are open questions listed under Other components.

families.summary: Legacy radar: a target passes when its physics-body mass S over distance exceeds 0.25 (d < 4 × S), up to a far plane about 15500 m ahead at the default saved FOV. FOV input 0.01 to 0.25 turns.

sections.title: Detection
sections.body:
Logic case 50 scores each candidate as S ÷ d, with S the target's physics-body mass and d the straight-line distance, and requires more than 0.25, so d < 4 × S. radar_range does not enter the score. It sets the far plane C = P × (0.75 + 0.25 × 0.01 ÷ saved radar_fov) instead: with P = 20000 and the saved default 0.1, C is about 15500 m.

On the sensor's axis a target passes within min(15500, 4 × S) m: 40 m for S = 10, 400 m for S = 100, 4000 m for S = 1000. Off the axis the straight-line distance can exceed C. The target must also lie inside four side planes set by the FOV. Candidates go best score first through a line-of-sight query, and the first that passes is output.

sections.title: Field of view and aim
sections.body: The FOV input is clamped to 0.01 to 0.25 turn and sets both the horizontal and the vertical field, 3.6 to 90 degrees. The tooltip's Max FOV 0.250 matches the code; the FOV port text says 0.125. Facing Yaw is clamped to -0.5 to 0.5 turn and Facing Pitch to -0.25 to 0.25 turn. Changing the FOV moves the side planes only: the far plane follows the saved radar_fov field, default 0.1.

sections.title: Height gates
sections.body: The radar runs only while its position is at least 0.25 m above a sampled height, and it sees only targets whose highest point is above y = 1. Reading that height as the water surface is an inference.

sections.title: Setup and interactions
sections.body: Outputs give distance in metres and angles in turns. They carry no SDK noise: radar_noise, radar_distance_noise and sonar_noise do not reach this logic case.
